title.zh: 卷237 列傳二十四 洪承畴 孟乔芳 张存仁
title.en: Volume 237 Biographies 24: Hong Chengchou, Meng Qiaofang, Zhang Cunren
title.raw: 卷237 列傳二十四 洪承畴 孟乔芳 张存仁

sentences.zh: 洪承疇，字亨九，福建南安人。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou, styled Hengjiu, was a native of Nan'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou, courtesy name Hengjiu, came from Nan'an in Fujian Province.

sentences.zh: 明萬曆四十四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the forty-fourth year of the Wanli reign of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the forty-fourth year of the Wanli era (1616).

sentences.zh: 累遷陝西布政使參政。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached the post of Assistant Administration Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to serve as vice commissioner of the Shaanxi provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，流賊大起，明莊​​烈帝以承疇能軍，遷延綏巡撫、陝西三邊總督，屢擊斬賊渠，加太子太保、兵部尚書，兼督河南、山、陝、川、湖軍務。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, when rebel bandits rose on a great scale, Emperor Zhuanglie of the Ming, seeing that Chengchou was skilled in military affairs, transferred him to be Grand Coordinator of Yan'an and Governor-General of the Three Borders of Shaanxi; he repeatedly attacked and beheaded rebel chieftains, was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, and concurrently supervised military affairs in Henan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign, as rebel armies swelled across the realm, the Chongzhen Emperor recognized Chengchou's military talent and appointed him grand coordinator of Yan'an and supreme commander of Shaanxi's three border districts. He repeatedly struck down rebel leaders, was made grand guardian of the heir apparent and minister of war, and given concurrent authority over forces in Henan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 時諸賊渠高迎祥最強，號闖王，李自成屬焉，承疇與戰，敗績。

translations.literal: At that time among the rebel chieftains Gao Yingxiang was the strongest, styled King Who Charges Through; Li Zicheng was subordinate to him. Chengchou fought him and suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Among the rebel leaders, Gao Yingxiang was then the most powerful, bearing the title King Who Charges Through, with Li Zicheng under his command. Chengchou met them in battle and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝擢盧像升總理河北、河南、山、陝、川、湖軍務，令承疇專督關中，復與自成戰臨潼，大破之，迎祥就俘。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanglie promoted Lu Xiangsheng to oversee military affairs in Hebei, Henan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Huguang, and ordered Chengchou to concentrate on supervising Guanzhong alone; Chengchou again fought Zicheng at Lintong and inflicted a great defeat on him, and Yingxiang was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongzhen Emperor elevated Lu Xiangsheng to direct military affairs across Hebei, Henan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Huguang, while assigning Chengchou sole responsibility for Guanzhong. Chengchou fought Li Zicheng again at Lintong, routed him decisively, and Gao Yingxiang was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 自成號闖王，分道入四川，承疇與屢戰輒勝。

translations.literal: Zicheng styled himself King Who Charges Through, divided his forces and entered Sichuan, and in repeated engagements with Chengchou he was invariably victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng now took the title King Who Charges Through, sent columns into Sichuan, and in repeated clashes with Chengchou he always came out on top.

sentences.zh: 自成還走潼關，承疇使總兵曹變蛟設伏邀擊，自成大敗，以十八騎走商洛。

translations.literal: Zicheng retreated toward Tong Pass; Chengchou had Regional Commander Cao Bianjiao set an ambush to intercept him. Zicheng suffered a great defeat and fled to Shangluo with eighteen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng fell back toward Tong Pass, Chengchou had regional commander Cao Bianjiao lay an ambush along his route. Zicheng was shattered and escaped to Shangluo with only eighteen riders.

sentences.zh: 關中賊略盡。

translations.literal: The bandits in Guanzhong were largely eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces in Guanzhong were nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 是歲為崇德三年。

translations.literal: That year was the third year of the Chongde reign.
translations.idiomatic: This took place in the third year of the Chongde era (1638).

sentences.zh: 太宗伐明，師薄明都，莊烈帝徵承疇入衛。

translations.literal: Taizong attacked the Ming; his army pressed close to the Ming capital, and Emperor Zhuanglie summoned Chengchou to come defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Taiji marched against the Ming and his forces neared the capital, the Chongzhen Emperor recalled Chengchou to reinforce the defense of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 明年春，移承疇總督薊、遼軍務，帥秦兵以東，授變蛟東協總兵、王廷臣遼東總兵、白廣恩援剿總兵，與山海馬科、寧遠吳三桂二鎮合軍；

translations.literal: In the spring of the following year Chengchou was transferred to be Governor-General of military affairs in Ji and Liaodong; he led Qin troops eastward, appointed Bianjiao Eastern Assistant Commander-in-Chief, Wang Tingchen Commander-in-Chief of Liaodong, and Bai Guang'en Commander-in-Chief for Relief and Suppression, and united his army with the two garrisons of Ma Ke at Shanhai and Wu Sangui at Ningyuan;
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Chengchou was reassigned as governor-general of Ji and Liaodong affairs and marched east at the head of his Shaanxi troops. He named Cao Bianjiao eastern assistant commander-in-chief, Wang Tingchen commander of Liaodong, and Bai Guang'en commander for relief operations, then combined forces with the garrisons of Ma Ke at Shanhaiguan and Wu Sangui at Ningyuan;

sentences.zh: 復命宣府楊國柱、大同王朴、密雲唐通各以其兵至：凡八總兵，兵十三萬，馬四萬，咸隸承疇。

translations.literal: He was further ordered that Yang Guozhu of Xuanfu, Wang Pu of Datong, and Tang Tong of Miyun should each bring his troops to join: in all eight commanders-in-chief, with 130,000 infantry and 40,000 horses, all subordinate to Chengchou.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned Yang Guozhu from Xuanfu, Wang Pu from Datong, and Tang Tong from Miyun, each with his own force. Eight regional commanders in all mustered 130,000 foot soldiers and 40,000 cavalry, all under Chengchou's command.

sentences.zh: 太宗師下大凌河，祖大壽入錦州為明守，松山、杏山、塔山三城相與為犄角。

translations.literal: Taizong's army descended on Dalinghe; Zu Dashou entered Jinzhou to defend it for the Ming, and the three cities of Songshan, Xingshan, and Tashan supported one another in a pincer formation.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji's forces took Dalinghe, after which Zu Dashou withdrew into Jinzhou to hold it for the Ming. Songshan, Xingshan, and Tashan formed a mutually supporting triangle of defenses.

sentences.zh: 承疇至軍，莊烈帝遣職方郎中張若麒趣戰，乃進次松山，國柱戰死，以山西總兵李輔明代。

translations.literal: When Chengchou reached the army, Emperor Zhuanglie sent Zhang Ruoqi of the Bureau of Military Appointments to urge battle; he then advanced and encamped at Songshan. Guozhu died in battle and Li Fuming, Commander-in-Chief of Shanxi, replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengchou joined the army, the Chongzhen Emperor sent Zhang Ruoqi from the Bureau of Military Appointments to press for action. Chengchou advanced and made camp at Songshan. Yang Guozhu fell in battle, and Li Fuming, commander of Shanxi, took his place.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，太宗自將御之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year Taizong personally led troops to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixth Chongde year (1640), Hong Taiji took the field in person to meet him.

sentences.zh: 上度松山、杏山間，自烏忻河南山至海，當大道立營。

translations.literal: The Emperor surveyed the ground between Songshan and Xingshan and, from the southern hills south of the Wuxin River to the sea, established camps astride the main road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reconnoitered the ground between Songshan and Xingshan and pitched camps along the main road from the hills south of the Wuxin River all the way to the sea.

sentences.zh: 承疇及遼東巡撫邱民仰率諸將駐松山城北乳峰山，步兵分屯乳峰山至松山道中為七營，馬兵分屯松山東、西、北三方，戰敗，移步兵近松山城為營，复戰又敗。

translations.literal: Chengchou and Qiu Minyang, Grand Coordinator of Liaodong, led the generals to encamp on Rufeng Hill north of Songshan city. The infantry were divided into seven camps along the road from Rufeng Hill to Songshan; the cavalry were posted east, west, and north of Songshan. They were defeated in battle, moved the infantry camps closer to Songshan city, fought again, and were defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou and Liaodong grand coordinator Qiu Minyang stationed their generals on Rufeng Hill north of Songshan. Infantry were spread in seven camps along the road from the hill to the city, cavalry on the eastern, western, and northern sides. After a defeat they drew the foot camps nearer the walls, fought again, and lost once more.

sentences.zh: 上誡諸將曰：「今夕明師其遁！

translations.literal: The Emperor admonished his generals, saying: "Tonight the Ming army will surely flee!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warned his commanders: "The Ming army will try to break out tonight!

sentences.zh: 」命諸軍當分地為汛以守，敵遁，視其眾寡，遣兵追擊，至塔山而止；

translations.literal: " He ordered the armies to hold assigned sectors as guard posts; if the enemy fled, they were to judge his numbers and dispatch troops in pursuit, stopping at Tashan;
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered each unit to hold its assigned sector. If the enemy fled, they were to gauge his strength, send pursuers, and drive him only as far as Tashan;

sentences.zh: 分遣諸將截塔山、杏山道及桑噶爾寨堡，又自小凌河西直抵海濱，絕歸路。

translations.literal: He dispatched generals separately to block the roads to Tashan and Xingshan and the fortress of Sanggar, and from west of the Xiaoling River straight to the seashore, cutting off the route of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments to seal the roads toward Tashan and Xingshan and the fortress of Sanggar, and posted troops from west of the Xiaoling River to the coast, cutting off every avenue of escape.

sentences.zh: 是夜三桂、樸、通、科、廣恩、輔明皆率所部循海引退，為我師掩殺，死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: That night Sangui, Pu, Tong, Ke, Guang'en, and Fuming all led their units in retreat along the coast and were ambushed and slaughtered by our army; the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: That night Wu Sangui, Wang Pu, Tang Tong, Ma Ke, Bai Guang'en, and Li Fuming all withdrew along the coast with their commands. Qing forces fell on them from ambush, and the dead were beyond number.

sentences.zh: 承疇、民仰率將吏入松山城守，上移軍松山，議合圍。

translations.literal: Chengchou and Minyang led the officers into Songshan city to defend it; the Emperor moved his army to Songshan and deliberated on completing the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou and Minyang withdrew with their officers into Songshan to hold the walls, while the emperor shifted his headquarters to Songshan and planned the final encirclement.

sentences.zh: 變蛟夜棄乳峰山寨，悉引所部馬步兵犯鑲黃旗汛地者一，犯正黃旗汛地者四，直攻上營，殊死戰，變蛟中創，奔還松山。

translations.literal: By night Bianjiao abandoned the stockade on Rufeng Hill and led all his cavalry and infantry in one assault on the guard post of the Bordered Yellow Banner and four assaults on the guard posts of the Plain Yellow Banner, striking straight at the Emperor's camp in a desperate fight; Bianjiao was wounded and fled back to Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: That night Cao Bianjiao abandoned the Rufeng stockade and hurled his entire force—once against the Bordered Yellow Banner line and four times against the Plain Yellow Banner—straight at the imperial camp in a desperate assault. Wounded, Bianjiao fell back to Songshan.

sentences.zh: 三桂、樸引餘兵入杏山。

translations.literal: Sangui and Pu led the remaining troops into Xingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui and Wang Pu led the survivors into Xingshan.

sentences.zh: 上遣諸將為伏於高橋及桑噶爾寨堡，明兵自杏山出奔寧遠，遇伏，殪強半。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent generals to lie in ambush at Gaoqiao and the fortress of Sanggar; the Ming troops issued from Xingshan fleeing toward Ningyuan, met the ambush, and more than half were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor posted ambushes at Gaoqiao and Sanggar. Ming troops breaking out of Xingshan toward Ningyuan ran into them, and more than half were cut down.

sentences.zh: 三桂、樸僅以身免。

translations.literal: Sangui and Pu barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui and Wang Pu escaped only with their own lives.

sentences.zh: 承疇師十三萬，死五萬有奇，諸將潰遁，惟變蛟、廷臣以殘兵萬餘從。

translations.literal: Of Chengchou's army of 130,000, more than 50,000 died; the generals broke and fled, and only Bianjiao and Tingchen followed him with somewhat more than 10,000 remnant troops.
translations.idiomatic: Of Chengchou's force of 130,000, over 50,000 were killed. The other commanders scattered in flight; only Bianjiao and Tingchen remained with a little more than 10,000 battered troops.

sentences.zh: 城圍既合，上以敕諭承疇降。

translations.literal: Once the encirclement of the city was complete, the Emperor sent an imperial edict urging Chengchou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege ring was complete, the emperor sent an edict calling on Chengchou to surrender.

sentences.zh: 九月，上還盛京，命貝勒多鐸等留護諸軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Emperor returned to Shengjing and ordered the princes Dorgon and others to remain and guard the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor returned to Mukden, leaving Princes Dorgon and others to oversee the siege forces.

sentences.zh: 承疇悉眾突圍，攻鑲黃旗擺牙喇阿禮哈超哈，戰敗，不能出。

translations.literal: Chengchou led his entire force in a breakout, attacking the Bordered Yellow Banner guard Alyahaqoha, was defeated, and could not get out.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou threw his whole garrison into a breakout against the Bordered Yellow Banner guard Alyahaqoha, was beaten back, and could not break the ring.

sentences.zh: 十月，命肅郡王豪格、公滿達海駐松山。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he ordered Prince Su Hooge and the duke Mandahai to garrison Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he assigned Prince Su Hooge and Duke Mandahai to hold Songshan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，承疇聞關內援師且至，復遣將以兵六千夜出攻正紅旗擺牙喇阿禮哈超哈及正黃旗蒙古營，戰敗，城閉不得入，強半降我師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, hearing that relief troops from within the passes were about to arrive, Chengchou again sent a general with 6,000 men by night to attack the Plain Red Banner guard Alyahaqoha and the Mongol camp of the Plain Yellow Banner; they were defeated, the gates were shut and they could not enter, and more than half surrendered to our army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, hearing that relief from inside the passes was near, Chengchou sent 6,000 men by night against the Plain Red Banner guard and the Plain Yellow Mongol camp. They were repulsed, the gates were barred against them, and more than half went over to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 餘眾潰走杏山，道遇伏，死。

translations.literal: The remainder broke and fled toward Xingshan; on the road they met an ambush and perished.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fled toward Xingshan, were caught in an ambush on the road, and were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝初以楊繩武督師援承疇，繩武卒，以范志完代，皆畏我師強，宿留不進。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanglie had first appointed Yang Shengwu to command the relief army for Chengchou; Shengwu died and Fan Zhiguan replaced him. Both feared the strength of our army and lingered without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongzhen Emperor had first named Yang Shengwu to lead the relief force for Chengchou. After Shengwu died, Fan Zhiguan took his place. Both men feared Qing strength and stalled without coming forward.

sentences.zh: 承疇被圍閱六月，食且盡。

translations.literal: Chengchou had been besieged for six months and provisions were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou had been under siege for six months, and food was running out.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，松山城守副將夏成德使其弟景海通款，以子舒為質。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year Xia Chengde, deputy defender of Songshan city, had his younger brother Jinghai open negotiations, offering his son Shu as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: The following second month, Songshan deputy defender Xia Chengde had his brother Jinghai negotiate surrender, pledging his son Shu as hostage.

sentences.zh: 我師夜就所守堞樹雲梯，阿山部卒班布里、何洛會部卒羅洛科先登，遂克其城，獲承疇、民仰、變蛟、廷臣及諸將吏，降殘卒三千有奇。

translations.literal: Our army by night set scaling ladders against the battlements they were defending; Banbuli of Ašan's command and Luoluo Ke of Hošoi's command were the first to ascend, and the city was taken. Chengchou, Minyang, Bianjiao, Tingchen, and the other officers were captured, and somewhat more than 3,000 remnant soldiers surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Qing troops raised scaling ladders against the walls by night. Banbuli of Ašan's detachment and Luoluo Ke of Hošoi's climbed first, and the city fell. Chengchou, Minyang, Bianjiao, Tingchen, and the other officers were taken, and a little over 3,000 survivors surrendered.

sentences.zh: 時為崇德七年二月壬戍。

translations.literal: The time was the renxu day of the second month of the seventh year of Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: This occurred on the renxu day of the second month of the seventh Chongde year (1642).

sentences.zh: 上命殺民仰、變蛟、廷臣，而送承疇盛京。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Minyang, Bianjiao, and Tingchen put to death, and sent Chengchou to Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Minyang, Bianjiao, and Tingchen executed and had Chengchou sent to Mukden.

sentences.zh: 上欲收承疇為用，命範文程諭降。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to win Chengchou over for service and ordered Fan Wencheng to urge him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to employ Chengchou and sent Fan Wencheng to persuade him to submit.

sentences.zh: 承疇方科跣謾罵，文程徐與語，泛及今古事，梁間塵偶落，著承疇衣，承疇拂去之。

translations.literal: Chengchou was sitting with bare head and feet, reviling them; Wencheng spoke with him slowly, ranging broadly over affairs ancient and modern. Dust from the rafters happened to fall on Chengchou's garment, and he brushed it away.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou sat barefoot with his hair loose, hurling abuse. Wencheng talked with him gently, ranging from antiquity to the present. Dust from the rafters drifted onto his robe, and he brushed it off.

sentences.zh: 文程遽歸，告上曰：「承疇必不死，惜其衣，況其身乎？

translations.literal: Wencheng hurried back and told the Emperor: "Chengchou will surely not die—if he values his garment, how much more his person?
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng hurried back and told the emperor: "Chengchou will not die for his cause—he brushed dust from his robe; will he not value his own life even more?

sentences.zh: 」上自臨視，解所禦貂裘衣之，曰：「先生得無寒乎？

translations.literal: " The Emperor came in person to see him, removed the sable fur coat he was wearing and put it on him, saying: "Sir, are you not cold?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor came in person, took off his own sable coat and draped it over Chengchou, saying: "Sir, are you not cold?

sentences.zh: 」承疇瞠視久，歎曰：「真命世之主也！

translations.literal: " Chengchou stared for a long time and sighed: "Truly a ruler destined by Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: " Chengchou stared a long while and sighed: "This is truly a ruler heaven has sent for the age!

sentences.zh: 」乃叩頭請降。

translations.literal: " He then knocked his head on the ground and asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " He then kowtowed and asked to submit.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，即日賞賚無算，置酒陳百戲，諸將或不悅，曰：「上何待承疇之重也！

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and that same day bestowed rewards beyond counting, set out wine and staged a hundred entertainments. Some of the generals were displeased and said: "Why does Your Majesty treat Chengchou with such weight!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and that same day heaped rewards upon him, set out a banquet, and staged a hundred performances. Some generals grumbled: "Why does Your Majesty honor Chengchou so highly?

sentences.zh: 」上進諸將曰：「吾曹櫛風沐雨數十年，將欲何為？

translations.literal: " The Emperor addressed the generals: "We have weathered wind and rain for decades—what did we intend?
translations.idiomatic: " He turned to the generals and said: "We have fought through wind and rain for decades—what were we fighting for?

sentences.zh: 」諸將曰：「欲得中原耳。

translations.literal: " The generals said: "To gain the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered: "To win the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 」上笑曰：「譬諸行道，吾等皆瞽。

translations.literal: " The Emperor laughed and said: "It is like walking a road—we are all blind.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor smiled: "It is like walking a road—we have all been blind.

sentences.zh: 今獲一導者，吾安得不樂？

translations.literal: Now we have gained a guide—how should I not rejoice?
translations.idiomatic: Now we have found a guide—how could I not rejoice?

sentences.zh: 居月餘，都察院參政張存仁上言：「承疇歡然幸生，宜令薙發備任使。

translations.literal: After somewhat more than a month, Zhang Cunren, Censorate Commissioner, memorialized: "Chengchou rejoices that his life was spared; he should be ordered to shave his head and be prepared for appointment and service.
translations.idiomatic: After a month had passed, Censorate commissioner Zhang Cunren memorialized: "Chengchou is glad to be alive; he should shave his head and be readied for office.

sentences.zh: 」五月，上御崇政殿，召承疇及諸降將祖大壽等入見。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month the Emperor held court in the Hall of Reverent Governance and summoned Chengchou and the surrendered generals including Zu Dashou to audience.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month the emperor held audience in the Hall of Reverent Governance and summoned Chengchou and the surrendered generals, including Zu Dashou.

sentences.zh: 承疇跪大清門外，奏言：「臣為明將兵十三萬援錦州，上至而兵敗。

translations.literal: Chengchou knelt outside the Great Qing Gate and memorialized: "Your servant was a Ming general who led 130,000 troops to relieve Jinzhou; when Your Majesty arrived our army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou knelt outside the Great Qing Gate and said: "I was a Ming general leading 130,000 men to relieve Jinzhou. When Your Majesty came, my army was broken.

sentences.zh: 臣入守松山，城破被獲，自分當死，上不殺而恩育焉。

translations.literal: Your servant entered Songshan to defend it; when the city fell I was captured and judged myself deserving of death, yet Your Majesty did not kill me but nourished me with grace.
translations.idiomatic: I withdrew into Songshan to hold it. When the city fell I was taken and expected death, yet Your Majesty spared me and showed me kindness.

sentences.zh: 今令朝見，臣知罪，不敢遽入。

translations.literal: Now I am ordered to audience; your servant knows his guilt and dares not enter hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Now I am summoned to audience. I know my offense and dare not enter at once.

sentences.zh: 」上使諭曰：「承疇言誠是。

translations.literal: " The Emperor sent word: "What Chengchou says is indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent word: "Chengchou speaks truly.

sentences.zh: 爾時與我交戰，各為其主，朕豈介意？

translations.literal: When you fought me then, each served his own lord—how should I take offense?
translations.idiomatic: When you fought me then, each of us served his own lord. Why should I bear a grudge?

sentences.zh: 且朕所以戰勝明兵，遂克松山、錦州諸城，皆天也。

translations.literal: Moreover, that I was able to defeat the Ming troops and take Songshan, Jinzhou, and the other cities was all Heaven's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, my victories over Ming forces and the capture of Songshan, Jinzhou, and the other cities were heaven's work, not mine alone.

sentences.zh: 天道好生，故朕亦恩爾。

translations.literal: Heaven's way loves life; therefore I also show you grace.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven loves life, and so I show you mercy as well.

sentences.zh: 爾知朕恩，當盡力以事朕。

translations.literal: Knowing my grace, you should exert your utmost in serving me.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing my kindness, you should serve me with all your strength.

sentences.zh: 朕昔獲張春，亦嘗遇以恩，彼不能死明，又不能事朕，卒無所成而死，爾毋彼若也！

translations.literal: I once captured Zhang Chun and also treated him with grace; he could neither die for the Ming nor serve me, and in the end accomplished nothing and died—do not be like him!
translations.idiomatic: I once captured Zhang Chun and treated him kindly too. He would neither die for the Ming nor serve me faithfully, and died having achieved nothing. Do not be like him!

sentences.zh: 」承疇等乃入朝見，命上殿坐，賜茶。

translations.literal: " Chengchou and the others then entered for audience, were ordered to ascend the hall and be seated, and were given tea.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengchou and the others then entered. They were seated on the dais and offered tea.

sentences.zh: 上語承疇曰：「朕觀爾明主，宗室被俘，置若罔聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Chengchou: "I observe that your Ming ruler, when members of the imperial clan were captured, treated it as though he had not heard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Chengchou: "I see that your Ming sovereign, when princes of the blood were taken prisoner, acted as if he had heard nothing.

sentences.zh: 將帥力戰見獲，或力屈而降，必誅其妻子，否亦沒為奴。

translations.literal: When generals fought with all their strength and were captured, or when their strength was exhausted and they surrendered, their wives and children were invariably put to death, or else enslaved.
translations.idiomatic: When generals fought hard and were captured, or surrendered after their strength gave out, their wives and children were always executed—or enslaved if spared.

sentences.zh: 此舊制乎，抑新制乎？

translations.literal: Is this an old institution, or a new one?
translations.idiomatic: Is that an old practice, or a new one?

sentences.zh: 」承疇對曰：「舊無此制。

translations.literal: " Chengchou replied: "There was no such institution in former times.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengchou answered: "There was no such rule in earlier times.

sentences.zh: 邇日諸朝臣各陳所見以聞於上，始若此爾。

translations.literal: Recently the court ministers each stated his view to inform the throne, and only then did it become thus.
translations.idiomatic: Only lately have ministers at court each offered his view to the throne, and matters have come to this.

sentences.zh: 」上因嘆謂：「君闇臣蔽，遂多枉殺。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon sighed and said: "The ruler is benighted and his ministers conceal the truth, and so many are wrongly killed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sighed and said: "When the ruler is blind and his ministers hide the truth, innocent people die in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 將帥以力戰沒敵，斥府庫財贖而還之可也，奈何罪其孥？

translations.literal: When generals exhaust their strength in battle and perish before the enemy, the treasury's wealth might be spent to ransom and return them—that would be fitting; why punish their wives and children?
translations.idiomatic: When generals die fighting to the last, the state could spend treasury funds to ransom them—that would be fitting. Why punish their families?

sentences.zh: 其虐無辜亦甚矣！

translations.literal: Their cruelty toward the innocent is indeed extreme!
translations.idiomatic: Their cruelty toward the innocent is extreme indeed!

sentences.zh: 」承疇垂涕叩首曰：「上此諭真至仁之言也！

translations.literal: " Chengchou, tears streaming, knocked his head and said: "Your Majesty's instruction is truly the speech of utmost benevolence!
translations.idiomatic: " Chengchou wept and kowtowed: "Your Majesty's words are the voice of true benevolence!

sentences.zh: 」上還宮，命宴承疇等於殿上。

translations.literal: " The Emperor returned to the palace and ordered a banquet for Chengchou and the others in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor withdrew and ordered a banquet for Chengchou and the others in the hall.

sentences.zh: 宴畢，使大學士希福等諭曰：「朕方有元妃之喪，未躬賜宴。

translations.literal: When the banquet was finished he had Grand Secretaries Hifu and others convey: "I am presently in mourning for the Primary Consort and have not personally bestowed the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: When the feast ended he had Grand Secretary Hifu and others explain: "I am in mourning for the primary consort and could not host you in person.

sentences.zh: 爾等勿以為意！

translations.literal: Do not take it to heart!
translations.idiomatic: Please do not take offense!

sentences.zh: 」承疇等復叩首謝。

translations.literal: " Chengchou and the others again knocked their heads in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengchou and the others kowtowed again in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝初聞承疇死，予祭十六壇，建祠都城外，與邱民仰並列。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie first heard that Chengchou had died, he granted sacrifices at sixteen altars and built a shrine outside the capital, where Chengchou was enshrined alongside Qiu Minyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor first heard that Chengchou had died, he ordered sacrifices at sixteen altars and built a shrine outside the capital with plaques for Chengchou and Qiu Minyang side by side.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝將親臨奠，俄聞承疇降，乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanglie was about to come in person to offer libations when he suddenly heard that Chengchou had surrendered, and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongzhen Emperor was about to attend the rites in person when word came that Chengchou had surrendered, and he called it off.

sentences.zh: 承疇既降，隸鑲黃旗漢軍，太宗遇之厚。

translations.literal: After Chengchou surrendered he was enrolled in the Han Military Bordered Yellow Banner, and Taizong treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had submitted, Chengchou was enrolled in the Han Chinese Bordered Yellow Banner, and Hong Taiji treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 然終太宗世，未嘗命以官。

translations.literal: Yet throughout Taizong's reign he was never appointed to office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet throughout Hong Taiji's lifetime he was never given an official post.

sentences.zh: 順治元年四月，睿親王多爾袞帥師伐明，承疇從。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Shunzhi, Prince Rui Dorgon led an army to attack the Ming, and Chengchou accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first Shunzhi year (1644), Prince Rui Dorgon marched against the Ming, and Chengchou went with him.

sentences.zh: 既定京師，命承疇仍以太子太保、兵部尚書兼右副都御史，同內院官佐理機務。

translations.literal: After the capital was secured he ordered Chengchou to retain his titles of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of War, and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and together with the Inner Court officials to assist in managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Beijing was taken, Chengchou was kept on as grand guardian of the heir apparent, minister of war, and vice censor-in-chief, and assigned with Inner Court officials to help run the government.

sentences.zh: 旋與同官馮銓啟睿親王，復明內閣故事，題奏皆下內閣擬旨，分下六科，鈔發各部院。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he and his colleague Feng Quan memorialized Prince Rui to restore the Ming Grand Secretariat precedent: all memorials and reports were sent down to the Grand Secretariat to draft rescripts, then distributed to the Six Offices of Scrutiny and copied out to the ministries and boards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and his colleague Feng Quan petitioned Prince Rui to restore the Ming Grand Secretariat practice: memorials went to the secretariat for draft rescripts, then to the six scrutiny offices and on to the ministries and boards.

sentences.zh: 九月，上至京師，與銓及謝升奏定郊廟樂章。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Emperor arrived at the capital; with Quan and Xie Sheng he memorialized to fix the ritual music for the suburban and temple sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor reached Beijing. With Feng Quan and Xie Sheng he submitted plans fixing the ritual music for suburban and temple sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二年，豫親王多鐸師下江南。

translations.literal: In the second year Prince Yu Dodo led his army south into Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Prince Yu Dodo marched into the lower Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 閏六月，命承疇以原官總督軍務，招撫江南各省，鑄「招撫南方總督軍務大學士」印，賜敕便宜行事。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month Chengchou was ordered, retaining his former offices, to be Governor-General of military affairs and to pacify and win over the provinces of Jiangnan; a seal was cast reading "Grand Secretary, Governor-General of Military Affairs for Pacifying the South," and an edict was bestowed authorizing discretionary action.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month Chengchou was ordered, with his existing titles, to direct military affairs and win over the Jiangnan provinces. A seal was cast reading "Grand Secretary, Governor-General for Pacifying the South," and he was given an edict to act at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 是時明唐王聿鍵稱號福建，其大學士黃道周率師道廣信、衢州向徽州，左僉都御史金聲家休寧，募鄉兵十餘萬屯績溪；

translations.literal: At this time the Ming Prince of Tang, Zhu Yujian, had proclaimed himself in Fujian; his Grand Secretary Huang Daozhou led troops from the Guangxin road toward Quzhou and Huizhou; Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Jin Sheng, a native of Xiuning, raised more than 100,000 local militia and encamped at Jixi;
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Tang, Zhu Yujian, had meanwhile proclaimed himself in Fujian. His grand secretary Huang Daozhou marched from the Guangxin route toward Quzhou and Huizhou. Left vice censor Jin Sheng of Xiuning raised more than 100,000 local militia and camped at Jixi;

sentences.zh: 諸宗姓高安王常淇保徽州，蘄水王術肸子常闒自號樊山王屯潛山、太湖間，由揾號金華王據饒州，誼石號樂安王、誼泐號瑞安王分屯溧陽、金壇、興化諸縣；

translations.literal: Among the imperial clansmen, Prince of Gao'an Zhu Changqi held Huizhou; Zhu Chang'an, son of the Prince of Qishui Zhu Shuxi, styled himself Prince of Fanshan and encamped between Qianshan and Taihu; Zhu Youwen styled himself Prince of Jinhua and held Raozhou; Zhu Yishi styled himself Prince of Le'an and Zhu Yile styled himself Prince of Ruian, and they divided their forces among the counties of Liyang, Jintan, Xinghua, and others;
translations.idiomatic: Among Ming princes, the Prince of Gao'an held Huizhou; Zhu Chang'an, son of the Prince of Qishui, styled himself Prince of Fanshan and camped between Qianshan and Taihu; Zhu Youwen styled himself Prince of Jinhua and held Raozhou; Zhu Yishi as Prince of Le'an and Zhu Yile as Prince of Ruian posted troops across Liyang, Jintan, Xinghua, and neighboring counties;

sentences.zh: 荊本徹以舟師駐太湖，敗，復入崇明：皆為明守。

translations.literal: Jing Benche stationed a fleet on Taihu, was defeated, and again entered Chongming—all holding out for the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Benche kept a fleet on Lake Tai, was beaten, and withdrew to Chongming—all still fighting for the Ming cause.

sentences.zh: 承疇至官，招撫江南寧國、徽州，江西南昌、南康、九江、瑞州、撫州、饒州、臨江、吉安、廣信、建昌、袁州諸府。

translations.literal: When Chengchou took up his post he pacified and won over the prefectures of Ningguo and Huizhou in Jiangnan, and in Jiangxi Nanchang, Nankang, Jiujiang, Ruizhou, Fuzhou, Raozhou, Linjiang, Ji'an, Guangxin, Jianchang, and Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Chengchou brought over Ningguo and Huizhou in Jiangnan and, in Jiangxi, Nanchang, Nankang, Jiujiang, Ruizhou, Fuzhou, Raozhou, Linjiang, Ji'an, Guangxin, Jianchang, and Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣提督張天祿，總兵卜從善、李仲興、劉澤泳等攻破績溪。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he dispatched Commissioner Zhang Tianlu and Commanders-in-Chief Bu Congshan, Li Zhongxing, Liu Zeyong, and others, who stormed and took Jixi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he sent Commissioner Zhang Tianlu with commanders Bu Congshan, Li Zhongxing, Liu Zeyong, and others, who stormed and took Jixi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，進破道周於婺源，聲、道周見獲，皆不屈，送江寧殺之；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he advanced and defeated Daozhou at Wuyuan; Sheng and Daozhou were captured, both refused to submit, and were sent to Jiangning and executed;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month his forces defeated Huang Daozhou at Wuyuan. Jin Sheng and Daozhou were taken, refused to submit, and were sent to Nanjing and executed;

sentences.zh: 總兵李成棟破崇明，本徹走入海，殺其將李守庫、徐君美。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Li Chengdong took Chongming; Benche fled to sea, and his generals Li Shouku and Xu Junmei were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Chengdong took Chongming. Benche fled to sea, and his generals Li Shouku and Xu Junmei were killed.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，遣總兵馬得功、卜從善等擊破司空寨，斬守寨石應璉、應璧等五人，獲常闒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year he dispatched Commanders-in-Chief Ma Degong and Bu Congshan and others, who stormed and took Sikong Stockade, beheaded the defenders Shi Yinglian, Yingbi, and three others, and captured Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year he sent commanders Ma Degong and Bu Congshan, who stormed Sikong Stockade, beheaded defenders Shi Yinglian, Yingbi, and three others, and captured Zhu Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 既，誼石、誼泐合兵二萬犯江寧。

translations.literal: Thereafter Yishi and Yile united 20,000 troops and attacked Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yishi and Yile combined 20,000 men and marched on Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 承疇先事誅內應西溝池萬德華、郭世彥、尤琚等八十餘人。

translations.literal: Chengchou had beforehand executed more than eighty collaborators within the walls, including Wan Dehua, Guo Shiyan, and You Ju of Xigouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou had already executed more than eighty collaborators inside the city, including Wan Dehua, Guo Shiyan, and You Ju of Xigouchi.

sentences.zh: 誼石等攻神策門，我分兵出朝陽、太平二門，截誼石等後，乃啟神策門出城兵奮擊，破之，追及攝山，斬馘無算。

translations.literal: Yishi and the others attacked the Shence Gate; we divided our forces and issued from the Chaoyang and Taiping gates to cut off Yishi's rear, then opened the Shence Gate and sent troops out in a fierce assault, routing them and pursuing to She Mountain, where heads taken and enemies slain were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yishi's force attacked the Shence Gate. Qing troops sallied from the Chaoyang and Taiping gates to cut off their retreat, then opened the Shence Gate and struck hard, routing them and pursuing to She Mountain with countless kills.

sentences.zh: 承疇疏請還京，以江南未大定，不允，賜其妻白金百、貂皮二百。

translations.literal: Chengchou memorialized asking to return to the capital; because Jiangnan was not yet fully pacified, permission was denied, and his wife was granted one hundred taels of silver and two hundred sable pelts.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou asked to return to the capital, but because Jiangnan was not yet fully pacified his request was denied; his wife was given one hundred taels of silver and two hundred sable pelts.

sentences.zh: 八月，征南大將軍貝勒博洛克金華，獲誼石。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Southern Expedition Commander-in-Chief, Prince Bolo Ke, took Jinhua and captured Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the southern expedition commander, Prince Bolo Ke, took Jinhua and captured Zhu Yishi.

sentences.zh: 九月，誼泐复犯江寧，承疇出禦，追獲誼泐及所置經略韋爾韜、總兵楊三貫、夏含章。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Yibo again invaded Nanjing; Hong Chengchou went out to meet the attack, pursued, and captured Yibo together with the grand coordinator he had appointed, Wei Ertao, and the regional commanders Yang Sangun and Xia Hanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yibo once more threatened Nanjing. Hong Chengchou marched out to repel him, ran him down, and took Yibo along with his appointed grand coordinator Wei Ertao and regional commanders Yang Sangun and Xia Hanzhang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，天祿搜婺源嚴杭山，獲常淇及所置監軍道江於東、職方司許文玠等。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Tian Lu searched Yanhang Mountain in Wuyuan and captured Chang Qi together with the military inspector he had appointed, Jiang Yudong, and the bureau officer Xu Wenji, among others.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Tian Lu swept Yanhang Mountain in Wuyuan and seized Chang Qi, along with Jiang Yudong, whom he had made military inspector, and Xu Wenji of the Bureau of Appointments, together with others in their party.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，從善及總兵黃鼎攻宿松，獲誼泐弟瑞昌王誼貴及所置軍師趙正；

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year Cong Shan and Regional Commander Huang Ding attacked Susong and captured Yibo's younger brother, the Prince of Ruichang Yigui, and the strategist he had appointed, Zhao Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Cong Shan and Regional Commander Huang Ding struck Susong, taking Yibo's brother, Prince Yigui of Ruichang, and his appointed strategist Zhao Zheng.

sentences.zh: 下饒州，獲由揾及其族人常洊、常沘、常涫：並請命斬之。

translations.literal: They took Raozhou and captured You Wen and his clansmen Chang Jian, Chang Bi, and Chang Guan; all were submitted with a request that they be executed by imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: Raozhou fell next, and with it You Wen and his kinsmen Chang Jian, Chang Bi, and Chang Guan; Hong Chengchou asked that all of them be put to death.

sentences.zh: 江南眾郡縣以次定。

translations.literal: The many prefectures and counties of Jiangnan were pacified in succession.
translations.idiomatic: One after another, the prefectures and counties of Jiangnan submitted to Qing rule.

sentences.zh: 明魯王以海轉徙浙、閩海中，號監國，明諸遺臣猶密與相聞。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Lu, Zhu Yihai, moved about the seas of Zhejiang and Fujian, styling himself regent, and the surviving ministers of Ming still maintained secret contact with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Lu, Zhu Yihai, wandered the coastal waters of Zhejiang and Fujian under the title of regent, while loyalist ministers of the fallen dynasty kept up clandestine ties with him.

sentences.zh: 是年四月，明給事中陳子龍家華亭，陰受魯王官，謀集太湖潰兵舉事。

translations.literal: That year in the fourth month the Ming supervising secretary Chen Zilong, a native of Huating, secretly accepted an office from the Prince of Lu and plotted to gather the scattered troops at Lake Tai to raise a rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of that year Chen Zilong, a former Ming supervising secretary from Huating, secretly took rank under the Prince of Lu and planned to rally the broken bands around Lake Tai for an uprising.

sentences.zh: 承疇遣章京索布圖往捕，子龍投水死。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou sent the clerk Suobutu to arrest him, and Chen Zilong drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou dispatched the clerk Suobutu to seize him, but Chen Zilong threw himself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 是月，柘林游擊陳可獲諜者謝堯文，得魯王敕封承疇國公，江寧巡撫土國寶為侯；

translations.literal: That month Chen Ke, vice commander at Zhailin, captured the spy Xie Yaowen and obtained the Prince of Lu's edict appointing Hong Chengchou Duke of the State and the Nanjing governor Tu Guobao marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the same month Zhailin vice commander Chen Ke took the spy Xie Yaowen and found among his papers a Prince of Lu patent making Hong Chengchou a duke and Nanjing governor Tu Guobao a marquis.

sentences.zh: 又得魯王將黃斌卿與承疇、國寶書；

translations.literal: He also obtained letters from the Prince of Lu's general Huang Binqing to Hong Chengchou and Tu Guobao.
translations.idiomatic: He also recovered correspondence from the Prince of Lu's general Huang Binqing addressed to Hong Chengchou and Tu Guobao.

sentences.zh: 鎮守江寧昂邦章京巴山、張大猷以聞。

translations.literal: The garrison commanders at Nanjing, Angbang Clerk Bashan and Zhang Dayou, reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Bashan, Angbang clerk charged with guarding Nanjing, and Zhang Dayou sent word of the discovery to the court.

sentences.zh: 上獎巴山等嚴察亂萌，命與承疇會鞫諜者，別敕慰諭承疇。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Bashan and the others for rigorously detecting the seeds of disorder, ordered them to join Hong Chengchou in jointly interrogating the spy, and issued a separate edict to comfort and reassure Hong Chengchou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended Bashan and his colleagues for sniffing out sedition in its infancy, told them to examine the spy together with Hong Chengchou, and sent Hong Chengchou a separate message of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 粵僧函可者，為故明尚書韓日纘子，日纘於承疇為師生。

translations.literal: The Cantonese monk Huan Ke was the son of the former Ming minister Han Rizuan, who in relation to Hong Chengchou had been teacher and student.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Ke, a monk from Guangdong, was the son of the former Ming minister Han Rizuan, who had once been Hong Chengchou's teacher.

sentences.zh: 函可將還裡，乞承疇畀以印牌護行出城，守者譏察笥中，得文字觸忌諱。

translations.literal: Huan Ke was about to return home and begged Hong Chengchou to give him a seal-plate pass to protect his travel out of the city; the guards inspected his trunk and found writings that violated taboo words.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Ke prepared to go home he asked Hong Chengchou for an official pass to see him safely through the gates; the guards searched his luggage and turned up texts that breached forbidden language.

sentences.zh: 巴山、張大猷以聞，承疇疏引咎，部議當奪職，上命貰之。

translations.literal: Bashan and Zhang Dayou reported this; Hong Chengchou submitted a memorial accepting blame, the board deliberated that he should be dismissed from office, and the emperor ordered that he be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Bashan and Zhang Dayou reported the matter. Hong Chengchou memorialized to take responsibility; the ministries recommended stripping him of office, but the emperor spared him.

sentences.zh: 承疇聞父喪，請解任守制，上許承疇請急歸，命治喪畢入內院治事。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou learned of his father's death and requested to leave his post to observe mourning; the emperor granted Hong Chengchou's request to return home urgently and ordered that after completing the funeral rites he enter the Inner Court to conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On news of his father's death Hong Chengchou asked to resign and mourn. The emperor allowed him to hurry home, directing that once the funeral was finished he should resume service in the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，還京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He came back to the capital in the fourth month of the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 六年，加少傅兼太子太傅，疏請定會推督、撫、提、鎮行保舉連坐法。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Junior Tutor and concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and submitted a memorial requesting the establishment of a system of joint recommendation with shared responsibility for governors-general, governors, provincial military commanders, and regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Junior Tutor and concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and memorialized for a joint nomination system under which sponsors of governors-general, governors, provincial commanders, and regional commanders would share punishment for bad picks.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「自後用督、撫、提、鎮，內院九卿咸舉所知。

translations.literal: They received an edict: "Henceforth, when appointing governors-general, governors, provincial military commanders, and regional commanders, all Nine Ministers of the Inner Court shall jointly recommend those they know.
translations.idiomatic: An edict came down: "From now on, whenever governors-general, governors, provincial commanders, or regional commanders are to be appointed, every minister of the Inner Court must put forward men he knows.

sentences.zh: 得人者賞，誤舉者連坐。

translations.literal: Those who recommend capable men shall be rewarded; those who wrongly recommend shall share punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Reward the man who names a good appointment; punish the man who names a bad one together with his nominee.

sentences.zh: 八年閏二月，命管都察院左都御史。

translations.literal: In the intercalary second month of the eighth year he was ordered to take charge as Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the leap second month of the eighth year he was appointed to head the Censorate as Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 尋甄別諸御史為六等，魏琯等二十二人差用，陳昌言等二人內升，張煊等十一人外轉，王世功等十七人外調，降黜有差。

translations.literal: Soon he classified all censors into six ranks: twenty-two including Wei Guan were assigned to different duties, two including Chen Changyan were promoted within the court, eleven including Zhang Xuan were transferred outside, seventeen including Wang Shigong were posted elsewhere, and demotions and dismissals varied.
translations.idiomatic: He then sorted the censors into six grades. Twenty-two men led by Wei Guan were reassigned to new posts; Chen Changyan and one other were promoted within the capital; Zhang Xuan and ten others were rotated out; Wang Shigong and sixteen others were transferred to provincial posts; demotions and dismissals followed in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 煊疏劾吏部尚書陳名夏，因及承疇嘗與名夏及尚書陳之遴集火神廟，屏左右密議逃叛；

translations.literal: Xuan submitted a memorial impeaching Minister of Personnel Chen Mingxia, also alleging that Hong Chengchou had once together with Mingxia and Minister Chen Zhilin gathered at the Fire God Temple, dismissed attendants, and secretly discussed fleeing in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan impeached Minister of Personnel Chen Mingxia and claimed that Hong Chengchou had once met Mingxia and Minister Chen Zhilin at the Fire God Temple, sent away their attendants, and secretly plotted defection.

sentences.zh: 承疇又嘗私送其母歸里。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou had also once privately sent his mother home to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: He further charged that Hong Chengchou had earlier sent his mother home without authorization.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上方狩塞外，巽親王滿達海居守，集諸王大臣會鞫。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived the emperor was hunting beyond the frontier; Prince Xun Mandahai remained to guard the capital and gathered princes and ministers for joint interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached court while the emperor was on a hunting expedition beyond the passes. Prince Xun Mandahai, left in charge, assembled the princes and senior officials to investigate.

sentences.zh: 承疇言：「火神廟集議，即議甄別諸御史定等差，非有他也。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou said: "The gathering at the Fire God Temple was precisely to discuss classifying censors and fixing rank distinctions—nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou answered, "Our meeting at the Fire God Temple was only to rank the censors and set their grades. There was no other purpose.

sentences.zh: 」並以送母未請旨引罪。

translations.literal: " He also took blame for sending his mother home without requesting permission.
translations.idiomatic: " He admitted as well that he had sent his mother home without first seeking leave.

sentences.zh: 名夏亦列辨，因坐煊誣奏，論死。

translations.literal: Mingxia also offered a detailed defense; as a result Xuan was found guilty of false impeachment and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mingxia answered point by point. Zhang Xuan was convicted of false accusation and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上雪煊冤，黜名夏。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor cleared Xuan's injustice and dismissed Mingxia.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward the emperor reversed Zhang Xuan's conviction and removed Chen Mingxia from office.

sentences.zh: 因諭：「承疇火神廟集議，事雖可疑，難以懸擬；

translations.literal: Accordingly he instructed: "Hong Chengchou's gathering at the Fire God Temple, though suspicious, cannot be presumed upon;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ruled: "Hong Chengchou's meeting at the Fire God Temple may look doubtful, but it cannot be treated as proof of treason;

sentences.zh: 送母歸原籍未奏聞，為親甘罪，情尚可原。

translations.literal: sending his mother to her native place without reporting it was a willing offense for his parent's sake—the circumstances may be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: as for sending his mother home without informing the throne, he accepted guilt out of filial duty, and that may be excused.

sentences.zh: 留任責後效。

translations.literal: Let him remain in office and hold him accountable for future results."
translations.idiomatic: He is to keep his post and prove himself by what he does hereafter."

sentences.zh: 」九年五月，承疇聞母喪，命入直如故，私居持服，賜其母祭葬。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year, when Hong Chengchou learned of his mother's death, he was ordered to continue attending court as before, observe mourning in private residence, and his mother's funeral honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the ninth year, after Hong Chengchou's mother died, he was told to keep his regular attendance at court while mourning privately at home, and imperial funeral honors were granted for his mother.

sentences.zh: 九月，達賴喇嘛來朝，上將幸代噶，待喇嘛至入覲。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Dalai Lama came to court; the emperor planned to visit Daiga and wait for the Lama's arrival for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Dalai Lama arrived at court. The emperor intended to travel to Daiga and receive him there.

sentences.zh: 承疇及大學士陳之遴疏諫，上為罷行，並遣內大臣索尼傳諭曰：「卿等以賢能贊密勿，有所見聞，當以時入告。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou and Grand Secretary Chen Zhilin remonstrated in a memorial; the emperor abandoned the trip on their account and dispatched Inner Minister Suoni to convey: "You, with talent and ability, assist in confidential affairs; whatever you observe should be reported in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou and Grand Secretary Chen Zhilin remonstrated against the journey, and the emperor gave it up. He sent Inner Minister Suoni with this message: "You serve me in close counsel because you are able men. Whatever you see or hear, tell me promptly.

sentences.zh: 朕生長深宮，無自洞悉民隱。

translations.literal: I grew up in the deep palace and cannot by myself thoroughly understand the people's hidden grievances.
translations.idiomatic: I was raised within the palace walls and cannot, on my own, know the people's hidden troubles.

sentences.zh: 凡有所奏，可行即行；

translations.literal: Whatever you memorialize, if feasible it shall be done at once;
translations.idiomatic: When you advise me, if your proposal can be carried out, I shall carry it out at once;

sentences.zh: 縱不可行，朕亦不爾責也。

translations.literal: even if not feasible, I will not hold you accountable."
translations.idiomatic: and even when it cannot, I will not blame you for it."

sentences.zh: 十月正月，調內翰林弘文院大學士。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year he was transferred to be Grand Secretary of the Inner Hanlin Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year he was moved to the post of Grand Secretary of the Inner Hanlin Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 明桂王由榔稱號肇慶，頻年轉戰，兵朁地蹙，至是居安隆所，雲南、貴州二省尚為明守。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Gui Zhu Youlang had proclaimed himself at Zhaoqing; after years of shifting battle his forces and territory gradually contracted, and by this time he resided at Anlong, while Yunnan and Guizhou provinces were still held for the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Gui, Zhu Youlang, had raised his banner at Zhaoqing. Years of war had worn his armies down and squeezed his territory until he held only Anlong, while Yunnan and Guizhou still flew the Ming flag.

sentences.zh: 諸將李定國、孫可望等四出侵略，南攻湖南南境諸州縣，東陷桂林，西據成都，兵連不得息。

translations.literal: Generals Li Dingguo, Sun Kewang, and others raided in all directions—south attacking the southern border prefectures and counties of Hunan, east capturing Guilin, west holding Chengdu—and warfare was unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo, Sun Kewang, and the other Ming generals struck on every front: south into the Hunan borderlands, east into Guilin, west as far as Chengdu. The fighting never let up.

sentences.zh: 五月，上授承疇太保兼太子太師、內翰林國史院大學士、兵部尚書兼都察院右副都御史，經略湖廣、廣東、廣西、雲南、貴州等處地方，總督軍務兼理糧餉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the emperor appointed Hong Chengchou Grand Preceptor and concurrent Grand Master of the Heir Apparent, Grand Secretary of the Inner Hanlin Guoshi Academy, Minister of War and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right of the Censorate, to serve as grand coordinator of Huguang, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou and other regions, with overall command of military affairs and supervision of grain supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor made Hong Chengchou Grand Preceptor and Grand Master of the Heir Apparent, Grand Secretary of the Inner Hanlin Guoshi Academy, Minister of War and Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right, and sent him to coordinate Huguang, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou, with full authority over campaigns and provisions.

sentences.zh: 敕諭撫鎮以下咸聽節制，攻守便宜行事。

translations.literal: An edict instructed that all officials below the level of governor and commander must obey his command and act at discretion in attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that every governor and commander beneath him must take his orders and act as local conditions required in attack or defense.

sentences.zh: 滿兵當留當撤，即行具奏。

translations.literal: Whether Manchu troops should remain or withdraw was to be reported immediately in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Decisions on keeping or withdrawing Manchu troops were to be reported at once.

sentences.zh: 命內院以特假便宜條款詳列敕書，宣示中外；

translations.literal: The Inner Court was ordered to set forth in detail in the imperial edict the special discretionary provisions and proclaim them within and beyond the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Court was told to spell out his special powers of discretion in the commission itself and publish them throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 並允承疇疏薦，起原任大學士李率泰督兩廣。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou's memorial recommendation was also granted, reappointing the former Grand Secretary Li Shuaitai to govern the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also accepted Hong Chengchou's recommendation and recalled former Grand Secretary Li Shuaitai to oversee the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 以江西寇未盡，命承疇兼領，鑄「經略大學士」印授之。

translations.literal: Because bandits in Jiangxi were not yet eliminated, Hong Chengchou was ordered to concurrently take charge, and a seal reading "Grand Coordinator Grand Secretary" was cast and conferred upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Since rebels in Jiangxi had not yet been cleared, Hong Chengchou was given concurrent authority there as well, and a seal inscribed "Grand Coordinator Grand Secretary" was cast for him.

sentences.zh: 臨發，賜蟒朝衣、冠帶、鞾襪、松石嵌撒袋、弓矢、馬五、鞍轡二，諸將李本深等八十七人朝衣、冠帶、撒袋、弓矢、刀馬、鞍轡有差。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure the emperor bestowed python robes, court hats, belts, boots and socks, sash-pouches inlaid with pine and turquoise, bow and arrows, five horses, and two sets of saddle and bridle; eighty-seven officers including Li Benshen received court robes, belts, pouches, bows, arrows, sabers, horses, and saddles in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out the emperor gave him python court robes, hat and belt, boots and socks, an inlaid sash-pouch, bow and arrows, five horses, and two saddled mounts. Eighty-seven officers led by Li Benshen received court dress, arms, horses, and harness in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 承疇至軍，疏言：「湖南駐重兵足備防剿，而各郡窵遠，兵力所不及。

translations.literal: When Hong Chengchou reached the army he submitted a memorial saying: "Hunan holds heavy troops sufficient for defense and suppression, yet the various prefectures are remote and deep, beyond what the forces can reach.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching headquarters Hong Chengchou wrote: "Hunan already has enough troops for defense and pursuit, but its prefectures lie far apart, and our strength cannot cover them all.

sentences.zh: 郝搖旗、一隻虎等竊伏湖北荊、襄諸郡，倘南窺澧、岳，則我軍腹背受敵。

translations.literal: Hao Yaoqi, One-Tiger, and others lie hidden in the Jing and Xiang prefectures of Hubei; if they peer south toward Li and Yue, then our army will be attacked front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yaoqi, One-Tiger, and their bands are lurking in the Jing and Xiang region of Hubei. If they strike south toward Li and Yuezhou, our forces will be caught between two enemies.

sentences.zh: 臣與督臣、議臣宜往來長沙四應調度。

translations.literal: Your minister together with the governor and deliberating officials ought to move back and forth at Changsha and respond on all four sides with deployment.
translations.idiomatic: I should therefore shuttle between Changsha and the front with the governor and staff, coordinating on every side.

sentences.zh: 督臣率提標兵駐荊州，別遣兵增武昌城守，以壯聲援。

translations.literal: The governor should lead the provincial banner troops to garrison Jingzhou and separately dispatch troops to reinforce the defense of Wuchang, so as to strengthen support by reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The governor should hold Jingzhou with the provincial banner force and send extra men to stiffen Wuchang's garrison, so our presence there remains credible.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「桂林雖復，李定國軍距桂林僅二百里，滿洲援剿官兵豈能定留？

translations.literal: " He also submitted a memorial saying: "Although Guilin has been recovered, Li Dingguo's army is only two hundred li from Guilin—how can the Manchu relief and suppression troops be fixed in place?
translations.idiomatic: " In another memorial he warned: "Guilin is back in our hands, but Li Dingguo sits only two hundred li away. We cannot keep the Manchu relief force there indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 克復州縣，何以分守？

translations.literal: When prefectures and counties are recovered, how can they be divided for garrison?
translations.idiomatic: Even if we retake surrounding districts, who will hold them?

sentences.zh: 又使孫可望诇我兵出援，潛自靖、沅截粵西險道，則我首尾難顧。

translations.literal: If Sun Kewang also scouts our troops going out in relief and secretly cuts the dangerous routes of western Guang from Jing and Yuan, then we shall find it hard to care for both head and tail.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kewang may watch for our columns to march out, then slip through Jing and Yuan to seize the mountain passes of western Guangxi, leaving us unable to protect both ends of the line.

sentences.zh: 置孤軍於徼外，其危易見。

translations.literal: To place an isolated army beyond the frontier—its danger is easy to see.
translations.idiomatic: Stationing a lone force on the outer edge of our territory is plainly perilous.

sentences.zh: 臣已分兵馳赴，俾佐戰守，且當親歷衡、永，察機宜以聞。

translations.literal: Your minister has already divided troops and sent them in haste to assist in fighting and defense, and should personally traverse Heng and Yong, observe what is opportune, and report.
translations.idiomatic: I have already detached troops to reinforce the garrison, and I mean to inspect Heng and Yong myself and report what course seems best.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，上授固山額真陳泰為寧南靖寇大將軍，及固山額真藍拜、濟席哈，擺牙喇纛章京蘇克薩哈等率師鎮湖南；

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month the emperor appointed Banner General Chen Tai Pacifier of the South and Queller of Bandits, together with Banner Generals Lanbai and Jixike and Baita Banner Commander Sukesaha and others to lead troops and garrison Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth month the emperor named Banner General Chen Tai Pacifier of the South and Queller of Bandits, with Banner Generals Lanbai and Jixike and Baita Banner Commander Sukesaha among others, to take an army into Hunan.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月，命靖南王耿繼茂率所部自廣州移鎮桂林：皆承疇疏發之也。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year he ordered Prince of Pacifying the South Geng Jingmao to lead his division from Guangzhou to transfer garrison to Guilin—all of this arose from Hong Chengchou's memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eleventh year he ordered Prince of Pacifying the South Geng Jingmao to move his troops from Guangzhou to Guilin. Each of these measures followed from Hong Chengchou's memorials.

sentences.zh: 是歲孫可望劫桂王，殺大學士吳貞毓等，方內訌。

translations.literal: That year Sun Kewang seized the Prince of Gui, killed Grand Secretary Wu Zhenyu and others, and was in the midst of internal strife.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Sun Kewang kidnapped the Prince of Gui, murdered Grand Secretary Wu Zhenyu and others, and plunged the Ming camp into civil discord.

sentences.zh: 十二年六月，可望遣劉文秀攻常德，分兵使盧明臣、馮雙禮攻武昌、岳州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year Sun Kewang sent Liu Wenxiu to attack Changde and divided his troops, sending Lu Mingchen and Feng Shuangli to attack Wuchang and Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twelfth year Sun Kewang dispatched Liu Wenxiu against Changde while Lu Mingchen and Feng Shuangli struck Wuchang and Yuezhou with separate columns.

sentences.zh: 承疇、陳泰遣蘇克薩哈迎擊，破之。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou and Chen Tai sent Sukesaha to meet and strike them and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou and Chen Tai sent Sukesaha to intercept the invaders and broke their force.

sentences.zh: 明臣墮水死。

translations.literal: Mingchen fell into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mingchen drowned.

sentences.zh: 文秀、雙禮皆走貴州。

translations.literal: Wenxiu and Shuangli both fled to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenxiu and Feng Shuangli both retreated into Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 陳泰旋卒於軍，以固山額真阿爾津為寧南靖寇大將軍，率固山額真卓羅、祖澤潤等分駐荊州、長沙。

translations.literal: Chen Tai soon died in the army; Banner General A'erjin was made Pacifier of the South and Queller of Bandits, leading Banner Generals Zhuoluo, Zu Zerun, and others to divide garrisons between Jingzhou and Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai died soon afterward in camp. Banner General A'erjin replaced him as Pacifier of the South and Queller of Bandits, with Banner Generals Zhuoluo, Zu Zerun, and others dividing command between Jingzhou and Changsha.

sentences.zh: 十三年，考滿，加太傅，仍兼太子太師。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, upon completion of his term of service, he was promoted to Grand Tutor while still retaining Grand Master of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when his term review came due, he was raised to Grand Tutor while keeping the title of Grand Master of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 李定國奉明桂王入雲南，湖廣無兵事。

translations.literal: Li Dingguo escorted the Ming Prince of Gui into Yunnan, and Huguang saw no military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo withdrew with the Ming Prince of Gui into Yunnan, and fighting in Huguang subsided.

sentences.zh: 阿爾津議以重兵駐辰州，謀自沅、靖入滇、黔，承疇與異議。

translations.literal: A'erjin proposed garrisoning heavy troops at Chenzhou and planning to enter Yunnan and Guizhou from Yuan and Jing; Hong Chengchou disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: A'erjin wanted a strong force at Chenzhou and planned to advance into Yunnan and Guizhou through Yuan and Jing, but Hong Chengchou opposed the scheme.

sentences.zh: 上召阿爾津還京師，以宗室羅託代。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned A'erjin back to the capital and replaced him with the imperial clansman Luo Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled A'erjin to the capital and sent the imperial clansman Luo Tuo in his place.

sentences.zh: 十四年，可望叛其主，舉兵攻雲南，與定國戰而敗；

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Sun Kewang rebelled against his lord, raised troops to attack Yunnan, fought with Dingguo and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Sun Kewang turned against his master, marched on Yunnan, and was beaten by Li Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詣長沙降。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he came to Changsha and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he went to Changsha and submitted.

sentences.zh: 時上已允承疇解任還京師養疴，至是命承疇留任，督所部與羅託等規取貴州，並命平西大將軍吳三桂自四川、征南將軍卓布泰自廣西分道入。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had already granted Hong Chengchou's request to leave his post and return to the capital to convalesce; now he ordered Hong Chengchou to remain in office, supervise his division together with Luo Tuo and others in planning the capture of Guizhou, and also ordered Pacifier of the West Wu Sangui to enter from Sichuan and Southern Expedition General Zhuobutai to enter from Guangxi by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already approved Hong Chengchou's request to leave office and recover his health in the capital, but now he told Hong Chengchou to stay on, direct his troops with Luo Tuo and the others to take Guizhou, and ordered Pacifier of the West Wu Sangui to advance from Sichuan while Southern Expedition General Zhuobutai came in from Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，復命信郡王多尼為安遠靖寇大將軍，帥師南征，於是承疇與羅託會師常德，道沅州、靖州入貴州境，克鎮遠。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year he again appointed Prince of Faith Duo Ni Pacifier of the Distant and Queller of Bandits to command the army on the southern expedition; thereupon Hong Chengchou joined forces with Luo Tuo at Changde, passed through Yuan and Jing prefectures into Guizhou territory, and captured Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year the emperor again named Prince of Faith Duo Ni Pacifier of the Distant and Queller of Bandits to lead the southern campaign. Hong Chengchou joined Luo Tuo at Changde, crossed Yuan and Jing into Guizhou, and took Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 卓布泰招南丹、那地、撫寧諸土司，下獨山州，會克貴陽。

translations.literal: Zhuobutai summoned the native chieftains of Nandan, Nadi, and Funing, took Dushan Prefecture, and together they captured Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuobutai won over the chieftains of Nandan, Nadi, and Funing, seized Dushan, and joined the main force in taking Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 三桂亦自重慶取遵義進攻開州、桐梓，以其師來會。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui also advanced from Chongqing through Zunyi to attack Kaizhou and Tongzi, and came with his army to join the rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui pushed out from Chongqing through Zunyi against Kaizhou and Tongzi, then marched his army in to link up with the others.

sentences.zh: 承疇上疏籌軍食，言：「貴州諸府、州、縣、衛、所僅留空城，即有餘糧，兵過輒罄。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou submitted a memorial planning army provisions, saying: "In the various prefectures, districts, counties, guards, and posts of Guizhou only empty cities remain; even if there is surplus grain, when troops pass it is exhausted at once.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou memorialized on supplies, reporting: "Guizhou's prefectures, districts, counties, guards, and posts are little more than empty shells. Whatever grain they still hold disappears the moment an army marches through.

sentences.zh: 惟省倉存米七千餘石、穀四千餘石，足支一月糧。

translations.literal: Only the provincial granary holds a little more than seven thousand shi of rice and a little more than four thousand shi of grain, enough to supply one month's rations.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial storehouses contain only about seven thousand shi of rice and four thousand shi of grain—enough for a single month.

sentences.zh: 臣所部兵，令分駐鎮遠、偏橋、興隆、清平、平越諸處。

translations.literal: The troops under your minister's command have been ordered to divide garrisons at Zhenyuan, Pianqiao, Xinglong, Qingping, Pingyue, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: I have spread my own troops among garrisons at Zhenyuan, Pianqiao, Xinglong, Qingping, Pingyue, and the like.

sentences.zh: 降兵暫駐三五日，改屯天柱、會同、黔陽諸縣及湖南沅州。

translations.literal: Surrendered troops are temporarily stationed for three to five days, then transferred to garrison at Tianzhu, Huitong, Qianyang counties and Yuan Prefecture in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered soldiers are being held only a few days before they are settled as garrison troops in Tianzhu, Huitong, Qianyang, and Yuan Prefecture in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 四川兵駐遵義，廣西兵駐獨山，使分地就糧。

translations.literal: Sichuan troops garrison Zunyi and Guangxi troops garrison Dushan, so that each may draw grain from its assigned territory.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan forces are posted at Zunyi and Guangxi forces at Dushan so each body of men can live off the land where it stands.

sentences.zh: 聞信郡王大兵自六月初發荊州，需糧多且倍蓰。

translations.literal: I hear that the great army of the Prince of Faith, setting out from Jingzhou at the beginning of the sixth month, will require grain in great quantity and several times over.
translations.idiomatic: I am told the Prince of Faith's main army will march from Jingzhou at the start of the sixth month and will need rations in amounts several times larger than ours.

sentences.zh: 貴州山深地寒，收穫皆在九月。

translations.literal: Guizhou's mountains are deep and its land cold; harvests all come in the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou is rugged and cold, and the harvest does not come until the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 臣方遣吏勸諭軍民須納今歲秋糧之半，並檄下沅州運糧儲鎮遠，又令常德道府具布囊、椶套、木架、繩索，思南、石阡諸府、州、縣、衛、所及諸土司募夫役，具工糈，以赴軍興。

translations.literal: Your minister is already sending officials to urge soldiers and people to deliver half of this year's autumn grain, and has also dispatched orders to Yuan Prefecture to transport grain and store it at Zhenyuan; he has further ordered the circuit and prefecture of Changde to prepare cloth sacks, palm-fiber covers, wooden frames, and ropes, and the prefectures, districts, counties, guards, posts, and native chieftains of Sinan, Shiqian, and elsewhere to recruit laborers and prepare workers' rations for the military effort.
translations.idiomatic: I am already sending officers to collect half of this year's autumn tax in grain, ordering Yuan Prefecture to haul stores to Zhenyuan, and telling Changde to furnish sacks, palm covers, frames, and rope. Sinan, Shiqian, and the other prefectures, districts, guards, posts, and native offices are being called on for porters, tools, and rations to meet the army's needs.

sentences.zh: 」九月，授武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory.
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth month he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 信郡王多尼師至，駐平越楊老堡，承疇、三桂、卓布泰皆會，議多尼軍出中路，經關嶺鐵索橋至雲南省城，行一千餘裡；

translations.literal: When Prince of Faith Duo Ni's army arrived it garrisoned Yanglaobao at Pingyue; Hong Chengchou, Wu Sangui, and Zhuobutai all met and agreed that Duo Ni's army should take the central route, passing the iron-chain bridge at Guanling to the provincial city of Yunnan—a march of more than one thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Faith Duo Ni's force reached Pingyue and encamped at Yanglaobao. Hong Chengchou, Wu Sangui, and Zhuobutai conferred and decided that Duo Ni should take the middle road over the iron-chain bridge at Guanling to the Yunnan provincial capital, a distance of more than a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 三桂軍自遵義經七星關，凡一千五百餘裡，先中路十日行；

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's army would go from Zunyi through Qixing Pass, altogether more than one thousand five hundred li, marching ten days ahead of the central route.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui would come from Zunyi by way of Qixing Pass, about fifteen hundred li in all, starting ten days before the center column.

sentences.zh: 卓布泰以南寧方有寇，自貴州、廣西邊境平浪、永順壩、威透山，出安隆所、黃草壩、羅平州，凡一千八百餘裡，先四川兵十五日行。

translations.literal: Because Nanning still had bandits, Zhuobutai would go from the Guizhou-Guangxi border at Pinglang, Yongshunba, and Weitoushan, out through Anlong, Huangcaoba, and Luoping Prefecture, altogether more than one thousand eight hundred li, starting fifteen days ahead of the Sichuan army.
translations.idiomatic: Since Nanning was still troubled by rebels, Zhuobutai would enter from the Guizhou-Guangxi frontier through Pinglang, Yongshunba, and Weitoushan, then by Anlong, Huangcaoba, and Luoping—a march of more than eighteen hundred li, fifteen days ahead of the Sichuan column.

sentences.zh: 既定議，承疇還貴陽，與羅託駐守，遣提督張勇等從多尼軍。

translations.literal: Once the plan was settled Hong Chengchou returned to Guiyang and garrisoned together with Luo Tuo, dispatching Provincial Commander Zhang Yong and others to follow Duo Ni's army.
translations.idiomatic: When the plan was fixed Hong Chengchou went back to Guiyang to hold the city with Luo Tuo and sent Provincial Commander Zhang Yong and others to march with Duo Ni.

sentences.zh: 明將李定國等拒戰皆敗，明桂王奔永昌。

translations.literal: The Ming generals Li Dingguo and others resisted in battle and were all defeated; the Ming Prince of Gui fled to Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo and the other Ming commanders fought and lost at every turn, and the Ming Prince of Gui fled to Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月乙未，三路師會​​，克雲南省城，明桂王奔緬甸。

translations.literal: On the yimwei day of the first month of the sixteenth year the three-route armies converged, captured the provincial city of Yunnan, and the Ming Prince of Gui fled to Burma.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimwei day in the first month of the sixteenth year the three columns united, took the Yunnan provincial capital, and the Ming Prince of Gui escaped into Burma.

sentences.zh: 承疇如雲南，疏言：「雲南險遠，請如元、明故事，以王公坐鎮。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou went to Yunnan and submitted a memorial saying: "Yunnan is perilous and remote; I request that, following the precedents of Yuan and Ming, a prince be seated there to hold the region.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou entered Yunnan and advised that, as under the Yuan and Ming, a prince should be stationed there to keep so distant and difficult a province.

sentences.zh: 」上以命三桂。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon assigned Wu Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor gave the post to Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 三月，承疇至雲南，疏言：「信郡王令貝子尚善及三桂等追剿至永昌、騰越。

translations.literal: In the third month Hong Chengchou reached Yunnan and submitted a memorial saying: "The Prince of Faith has ordered Prince Suoshan and Wu Sangui and others to pursue and suppress as far as Yongchang and Tengyue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Hong Chengchou arrived in Yunnan and reported: "The Prince of Faith has sent Prince Suoshan, Wu Sangui, and the others in pursuit as far as Yongchang and Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 明將賀九義、李成爵、李如碧、廖魚、鄒自貴、馬得鳴輩收集潰兵，分遁元江、順寧、雲龍、瀾滄、麗江，處處窺伺。

translations.literal: The Ming generals He Jiuyi, Li Chengjue, Li Rubi, Liao Yu, Zou Zigui, Ma Deming, and others gathered scattered troops and dispersed separately into Yuanjiang, Shunning, Yunlong, Lancang, and Lijiang, watching everywhere for openings.
translations.idiomatic: Ming commanders He Jiuyi, Li Chengjue, Li Rubi, Liao Yu, Zou Zigui, Ma Deming, and others have rallied broken units and slipped away toward Yuanjiang, Shunning, Yunlong, Lancang, and Lijiang, waiting for a chance to strike.

sentences.zh: 民間遭兵火，重以饑饉，近永昌諸處被禍更烈，週數百里杳無人煙，省城米價石至十三兩有奇。

translations.literal: Among the people war and fire have been added to famine; near Yongchang and other places the calamity has been still fiercer, and for several hundred li around there is no human smoke; in the provincial city the price of rice has reached more than thirteen taels per shi.
translations.idiomatic: The countryside has suffered war on top of famine. Around Yongchang the ruin is worst: for hundreds of li there is hardly a living soul, and in the provincial capital rice now sells for more than thirteen taels a shi.

sentences.zh: 諸軍就糧宜良、富民、羅次、姚安、賓川、臨安、新興、澂江、陸涼諸處。

translations.literal: The various armies should draw grain at Yiliang, Fumin, Luoci, Yao'an, Binchuan, Lin'an, Xingxing, Chengjiang, and Luliang.
translations.idiomatic: The troops should be fed from Yiliang, Fumin, Luoci, Yao'an, Binchuan, Lin'an, Xingxing, Chengjiang, and Luliang.

sentences.zh: 上明察萬里，自有宸斷，俾邊臣得以遵奉。

translations.literal: Your majesty sees clearly for ten thousand li and will have your own sage decision, so that border officials may obey and carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty sees farther than any border officer can, and I trust you will decide as you think best so that we on the frontier may follow your will.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上命戶部發帑三十萬，以十五萬賑兩省貧民，十五萬命承疇收貯，備軍餉不給。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered the emperor ordered the Ministry of Revenue to disburse three hundred thousand taels from the treasury, of which one hundred fifty thousand were to relieve the poor of the two provinces and one hundred fifty thousand were ordered to be received and stored by Hong Chengchou as a reserve against failure of army rations.
