translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached court the emperor told the Ministry of Revenue to release three hundred thousand taels from the treasury: half to feed the poor of the two provinces, and half for Hong Chengchou to hold in reserve against any break in the army's supplies.

sentences.zh: 八月，承疇疏言：「兵部密諮令速攻緬甸。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Hong Chengchou submitted a memorial saying: "The Ministry of War secretly advised ordering a rapid attack on Burma.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Hong Chengchou memorialized the throne: "The Ministry of War had privately urged that Burma be attacked at once.

sentences.zh: 臣受任經略，目擊民生彫敝，及土司降卒尚懷觀望，以為須先安內，乃可剿外。

translations.literal: Your servant, having received appointment as grand coordinator, has witnessed the people's livelihood battered and exhausted, and the native chiefs and surrendered troops still harbor wait-and-see attitudes; I hold that one must first secure the interior before one can suppress the outer enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking up my post as grand coordinator I have seen the people worn to the bone and the native chiefs and surrendered soldiers still holding back; we must settle affairs at home before we can strike beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 李定國等竄伏孟艮諸處，山川險阻，兼瘴毒為害，必待霜降始消，明年二月青草將生，瘴即復起，其間可以用師不過四月，慮未能窮追。

translations.literal: Li Dingguo and others lurk in Menggen and other places; the mountains and rivers are perilous and obstructive, and malarial poisons moreover cause harm; one must wait until the frost descends before they subside; in the second month of next year, when green grass sprouts, the miasma will rise again; within that span troops can be deployed for at most four months—I fear we cannot run them down to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo and his followers are hiding in Menggen and the like, where steep country and fever country alike block the way. The miasma does not lift until the frosts come; by the second month of next year, when fresh grass appears, it returns. We would have at most four months to campaign, and I doubt we could finish the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 定國等覬自景東、元江復入廣西，要結諸土司，私授劄印，歃血為盟。

translations.literal: Dingguo and others aspire to re-enter Guangxi from Jingdong and Yuanjiang, to win over the various native chiefs, privately confer letters and seals, and seal alliances with blood.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo and his men aim to slip back into Guangxi through Jingdong and Yuanjiang, rally the native chiefs, hand out seals in secret, and bind them with blood oaths.

sentences.zh: 若聞我師西進，必且避實就虛，合力內犯。

translations.literal: If they hear our army advancing westward, they will surely avoid the solid and strike the empty, joining forces to invade inward.
translations.idiomatic: Once they learn that our main force is marching west, they will dodge our strength and strike where we are weak, then turn and raid inward together.

sentences.zh: 我軍相隔已遠，不能回顧；

translations.literal: Our armies are already far apart and cannot look back;
translations.idiomatic: Our columns would already be too far apart to wheel about;

sentences.zh: 省城留兵，亦未遑堵禦：致定國等縱逸，所關非細。

translations.literal: the troops left at the provincial capital also have no leisure to block and defend: causing Dingguo and others to slip away—the matter is no small one.
translations.idiomatic: and the garrison left in the provincial capital would have no time to plug every gap—Dingguo and his party could break loose, with grave consequences.

sentences.zh: 臣審度時勢，權其輕重，謂今歲秋冬宜暫停進兵，俾雲南迤西殘黎，稍藉秋收以延餘喘；

translations.literal: Your servant has assessed the times and weighed what is heavy and light, and holds that this autumn and winter we should temporarily halt the advance of troops, so that the surviving people of western Yunnan may slightly rely on the autumn harvest to prolong their last breath;
translations.idiomatic: I have weighed the moment and believe we should suspend operations this autumn and winter, so the battered people of far western Yunnan can eke out a little life from the harvest;

sentences.zh: 明年盡力春耕，漸圖生聚。

translations.literal: next year exert all effort in spring plowing, and gradually seek to restore population and prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: next year plow hard in spring and slowly rebuild households and fields.

sentences.zh: 我軍亦得養銳蓄威，居中制外，俾定國等不能窺動靜以潛逃，諸土司不能伺間隙以思逞。

translations.literal: Our army will also be able to nurture sharpness and store up might, holding the center to control the outer regions, so that Dingguo and others cannot spy our movements to slip away in secret, and the native chiefs cannot watch for openings to think of acting out.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops meanwhile can rest, gather strength, and hold the center while controlling the periphery, so Dingguo cannot watch our movements and steal away and the native chiefs cannot seize a gap to make trouble.

sentences.zh: 絕殘兵之勾結，斷降卒之反側，則飢飽勞逸皆在於我。

translations.literal: Cut off the collusion of remnant troops, sever the wavering of surrendered soldiers—then hunger and fullness, weariness and rest all lie in our hands.
translations.idiomatic: Break the remnant soldiers' ties, cut off the surrendered troops' chance to turn—then whether they hunger or eat, tire or rest, all will depend on us.

sentences.zh: 定國等潛藏邊界，無居無食，瘴癘相侵，內變易生，機有可俟。

translations.literal: Dingguo and others hide along the borderlands with no dwelling and no food; malarial miasmas assail one another, internal mutiny easily arises—an opportunity may be waited for.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo and his men, crouching on the frontier without shelter or supplies, will be worn down by fever and privation until rebellion within their ranks becomes likely—time itself may serve us.

sentences.zh: 是時芻糧輳備，苗、蠻輯服，調發將卒，次第齊集，然後進兵，庶為一勞永逸、安內剿外長計。

translations.literal: At that time fodder and grain will be gathered in readiness, the Miao and Man will submit in harmony, generals and soldiers will be mobilized and assemble in order—then advance troops; thus may it be a long plan to secure the interior and suppress the exterior in one effort bringing lasting ease.
translations.idiomatic: By then fodder and grain can be stockpiled, the Miao and Man brought to heel, and officers and men called up and mustered in turn before we advance—a lasting policy of pacifying within while striking without, settled once for all.

sentences.zh: 」疏下議政王、貝勒、大臣會議，如所請暫停進兵。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the Prince Regent, princes, and ministers for joint deliberation, and as requested they temporarily halted the advance of troops.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial went to the Prince Regent, the princes, and the ministers for consultation, and as Hong Chengchou had asked they suspended the advance.

sentences.zh: 十月，以目疾乞解任，命回京調理。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, citing eye disease he requested relief from office and was ordered to return to the capital to recuperate.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he asked to be relieved on account of eye trouble and was told to return to Beijing to recover.

sentences.zh: 明年，三桂進兵攻緬甸，獲明桂王以歸。

translations.literal: The next year Wu Sangui advanced troops to attack Burma and captured the Ming Prince of Gui and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wu Sangui marched into Burma, took the Ming Prince of Gui prisoner, and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 語見三桂傳。

translations.literal: The account appears in Wu Sangui's biography.
translations.idiomatic: That story is told in the biography of Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，承疇乞致仕，予三等阿達哈哈番世職。

translations.literal: When the Shengzu ascended the throne, Hong Chengchou requested retirement and was granted a hereditary third-class adaha hafan rank.
translations.idiomatic: After the Kangxi Emperor came to the throne, Hong Chengchou asked to retire and was given a hereditary third-class adaha hafan.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年二月，卒，諡文襄。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Kangxi he died, posthumous title Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of Kangxi 4 and was posthumously titled Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 子士欽，順治十二年進士，官至太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: His son Shi Qin became a jinshi in the twelfth year of Shunzhi and rose to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi Qin passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of the Shunzhi reign and served as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 夏成德，廣寧人。

translations.literal: Xia Chengde was a native of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Chengde came from Guangning.

sentences.zh: 既，以鬆山降，隸正白旗漢軍。

translations.literal: Subsequently, having surrendered at Songshan, he was enrolled in the Han Army of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after surrendering at Songshan, he was placed in the Han Army of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治初，授三等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shunzhi reign he was appointed third-class angbang janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi reign he was made a third-class angbang janggin.

sentences.zh: 其弟景海，授一等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jinghai was appointed first-class jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jinghai received the rank of first-class jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 出為山東沂水總兵，嘗疏請收沂州明大學士張四知等財產，又越職乞頒方印，皆不得請。

translations.literal: He went out as regional commander of Yishui in Shandong; he once memorialized requesting confiscation of the property of the Ming grand secretary Zhang Sizhi and others of Yizhou, and also overstepped his duties in begging for a square seal to be issued—all were denied.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as regional commander at Yishui in Shandong, he once asked to seize the estates of the Ming grand secretary Zhang Sizhi and others at Yizhou and also overreached his office by begging for an official square seal; both requests were refused.

sentences.zh: 旋以縱所部越境暴掠，與青州道韓方昭互揭，還京師，卒。

translations.literal: Soon after, for allowing his troops to cross the border on violent pillage and mutually impeaching the Qingzhou intendant Han Fangzhao, he was recalled to the capital and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to the capital after letting his men raid across the border and trading accusations with the Qingzhou intendant Han Fangzhao, and died there.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定封三等子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign the fief was fixed as third-class zi.
translations.idiomatic: In early Qianlong his line was fixed with the hereditary rank of third-class viscount.

sentences.zh: 孟喬芳，字心亭，直隸永平人。

translations.literal: Meng Qiaofang, styled Xinting, was a native of Yongping in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qiaofang, courtesy name Xinting, came from Yongping in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 父國用，明寧夏總兵官。

translations.literal: His father Guoyong was regional commander of Ningxia under the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guoyong had been the Ming regional commander at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 喬芳仕明為副將，坐事罷，家居。

translations.literal: Qiaofang served the Ming as vice general; dismissed on account of an offense, he lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qiaofang had served the Ming as a vice general, but after being dismissed for an offense he lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 天聰四年，太宗克永平，喬芳及知縣張養初、家居兵備道白養粹、罷職副將楊文魁、游擊楊聲遠等十五人出降，命以養粹為巡撫，養初為知府，喬芳、文魁仍為副將，率降兵從諸貝勒城守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancong, when Taizong captured Yongping, Qiaofang together with the district magistrate Zhang Yangchu, the home-dwelling defense circuit intendant Bai Yangcui, the dismissed vice general Yang Wenkui, the battalion commander Yang Shengyuan, and ten others—a party of fifteen in all—came out and surrendered; he ordered Yangcui to be grand coordinator, Yangchu prefectural magistrate, Qiaofang and Wenkui to remain vice generals, and they led surrendered troops to follow the princes in holding the cities.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 4, when Hong Taiji took Yongping, Meng Qiaofang joined the district magistrate Zhang Yangchu, the retired defense intendant Bai Yangcui, the dismissed vice general Yang Wenkui, the battalion commander Yang Shengyuan, and ten others—fifteen men in all—in surrendering. Hong Taiji made Yangcui grand coordinator and Yangchu prefect, kept Meng Qiaofang and Wenkui as vice generals, and had them lead the surrendered troops in garrison duty under the princes.

sentences.zh: 上移軍向山海關，諸貝勒率喬芳、文魁、聲遠入謁行營，上召三人者酌以金卮，且諭之曰：「朕不似爾明主，凡我臣僚，皆令侍坐，吐衷曲，同飲食也。

translations.literal: The Emperor moved his army toward Shanhaiguan; the princes led Qiaofang, Wenkui, and Shengyuan to enter and audience at the mobile encampment; the Emperor summoned the three, poured for them from a golden goblet, and admonished them, saying: "I am not like your Ming lord: all my ministers I let sit in attendance, speak their innermost thoughts, and eat and drink together.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched toward Shanhaiguan, the princes brought Meng Qiaofang, Yang Wenkui, and Yang Shengyuan to audience at the field camp. He called the three forward, poured wine for them from a golden cup, and said: "I am not like your Ming sovereign. With me every officer sits at ease, speaks plainly, and shares food and drink.

sentences.zh: 」喬芳使诇陽和，而明總兵祖大壽亦使詣喬芳诇我師，喬芳縛以獻。

translations.literal: " Qiaofang sent men to reconnoiter Yanghe, while the Ming regional commander Zu Dashou also sent men to Qiaofang to spy on our army; Qiaofang bound them and presented them as captives.
translations.idiomatic: " Meng Qiaofang sent scouts to Yanghe, but the Ming commander Zu Dashou had also sent men to Meng Qiaofang to spy on our forces; Meng Qiaofang seized them and handed them over.

sentences.zh: 五月，明兵取灤州，貝勒阿敏棄永平出塞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Ming troops took Luanzhou; Prince Amin abandoned Yongping and went beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Ming recovered Luanzhou, and Prince Amin abandoned Yongping and withdrew beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 瀕發，屠城民，諸降官養粹、養初等死者十一人，喬芳、文魁、聲遠及郎中陳此心得免。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he slaughtered the city's people; among the surrendered officials Yangcui, Yangchu, and others eleven died; Qiaofang, Wenkui, Shengyuan, and the bureau director Chen Cixin escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he massacred the townspeople. Eleven of the surrendered officials, including Yangcui and Yangchu, were killed; Meng Qiaofang, Wenkui, Shengyuan, and the bureau director Chen Cixin survived.

sentences.zh: 喬芳從師還，隸烏真超哈為牛錄額真。

translations.literal: Qiaofang returned with the army and was enrolled in the ujen chaha as niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qiaofang marched back with the army and was registered in the ujen chaha as a niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，置六部，以喬芳為刑部漢承政，授世職二等參將。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year the Six Ministries were established; Qiaofang was made Han Supervisor of the Ministry of Punishments and granted a hereditary second-class colonel rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year, when the Six Ministries were set up, he was appointed Han supervisor of the Ministry of Punishments with a hereditary second-class colonel's rank.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年，更定官制，改左參政。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde the official system was revised and he was changed to Left Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 3, after the offices were reorganized, he became left vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，烏真超哈析置八旗四固山，以喬芳兼領正紅、鑲紅兩旗梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the ujen chaha was split and the Eight Banners' four gūsa were established; Qiaofang was concurrently appointed meile ejen of the Plain Red and Bordered Red Banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the ujen chaha was divided into four gūsa for the Eight Banners, and Meng Qiaofang was made meile ejen of both the Plain Red and Bordered Red Banners.

sentences.zh: 七年，從伐明，克塔山城。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed the campaign against the Ming and captured Tashan city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he joined the campaign against the Ming and took Tashan.

sentences.zh: 烏真超哈八旗复析置八固山，改鑲紅旗梅勒額真，遂為漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: The ujen chaha Eight Banners were again split into eight gūsa; he was changed to meile ejen of the Bordered Red Banner and thus became a member of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the ujen chaha Eight Banners were further divided into eight gūsa, he became meile ejen of the Bordered Red Banner and henceforth counted as Han Army Bordered Red.

sentences.zh: 八年，或訴貝勒羅洛渾家人奪金，喬芳置不問，坐瞻徇，降世職三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year someone complained that Prince Ruluohun's household had seized gold; Qiaofang ignored it and was punished for favoritism, his hereditary rank reduced to third-class jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when men accused Prince Ruluohun's household of seizing gold, Meng Qiaofang took no action and was punished for shielding them; his hereditary rank was cut to third-class jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 旋以從克前屯衛、中後所二城，加半個前程。

translations.literal: Soon after, for following in the capture of Qiandun Guard and the two fortresses of Zhonghou, he was given an addition of half a rank advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon rewarded with half a step of rank for helping take Qiandun Guard and the two posts at Zhonghou.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，入關，改左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, upon entering the pass, he was changed to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Shunzhi reign, after the entry into China proper, he was made left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 從諸軍西討。

translations.literal: He followed the various armies in the western punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He marched west with the main armies on the punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，以兵部右侍郎兼右副都御史，總督陝西三邊。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, as Right Vice Minister of War and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right, he was governor-general of the Three Borders of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shunzhi 2 he was appointed right vice minister of war and concurrent right vice censor-in-chief, with the title governor-general of Shaanxi's three border districts.

sentences.zh: 時張獻忠尚據四川，關中群盜並起，叛將賀珍躪漢中、興安諸府。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Xianzhong still held Sichuan, bandits rose together throughout Guanzhong, and the rebel general He Zhen trampled Hanzhong, Xing'an, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong still held Sichuan, rebels were rising all over Guanzhong, and the turncoat He Zhen was ravaging Hanzhong, Xing'an, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，武大定叛固原，徒黨甚眾。

translations.literal: That winter Wu Dading rebelled at Guyuan; his followers were extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Wu Dading rose at Guyuan with a very large following.

sentences.zh: 初，上命內大臣何洛會帥師鎮西安，至是就拜定西大將軍，遣固山額真巴顏、李國翰將禁旅濟師。

translations.literal: Initially the Shunzhi Emperor had ordered Inner Minister He Luohui to command troops garrisoning Xi'an; at this time he was directly appointed General Who Pacifies the West, and gūsa ejen Bayan and Li Guohan were dispatched to lead the forbidden brigade to reinforce the army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Shunzhi Emperor had put Inner Minister He Luohui in command at Xi'an; now he was formally made General Who Pacifies the West, and the gūsa ejen Bayan and Li Guohan were sent with the imperial guard to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 三年，复敕靖遠大將軍肅親王豪格帥師督諸將自漢中、興安入四川取獻忠，喬芳於其間亦分遣所部四出捕治。

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor again ordered General Who Pacifies the Remote Prince Su Hooge to lead troops supervising the generals to enter Sichuan from Hanzhong and Xing'an to take Xianzhong; meanwhile Qiaofang also dispatched his units in all directions to capture and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the court again ordered Prince Su Hooge, as General Who Pacifies the Distant, to lead the generals from Hanzhong and Xing'an into Sichuan against Zhang Xianzhong, while Meng Qiaofang sent his own detachments out in every direction to hunt down and pacify rebels.

sentences.zh: 初上官，長安民胡守龍者挾左道惑民，妄改元清光，將為亂，喬芳遣副將陳德捕誅守龍，散其脅從。

translations.literal: When he first took office, among the people of Chang'an one Hu Shoulong practiced heterodox arts to delude the populace, rashly changed the era name to Qingguang, and was about to rebel; Qiaofang sent Deputy General Chen De to capture and execute Shoulong and disperse those he had coerced into following him.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after assuming his post, Qiaofang learned that a Chang'an man named Hu Shoulong was using occult teachings to mislead the people, had presumptuously declared a new reign title, Qingguang, and was preparing to rise in revolt. Qiaofang dispatched Deputy General Chen De to seize and put Shoulong to death, then break up his intimidated followers.

sentences.zh: 是年春，賀珍與其徒孫守法、胡向化等以七萬人攻西安。

translations.literal: That spring, He Zhen together with his followers Sun Shoufa, Hu Xianghua, and others attacked Xi'an with seventy thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of that year, He Zhen marched on Xi'an at the head of seventy thousand men, accompanied by his lieutenants Sun Shoufa, Hu Xianghua, and others.

sentences.zh: 何洛會主城守，喬芳遣德軍西門，副將任珍軍北門，往來衝突，會李國翰師至，賀珍敗走。

translations.literal: Heluoai defended the main city; Qiaofang sent De's army to the west gate and Deputy General Ren Zhen's army to the north gate, and they clashed back and forth; when Li Guohan's army arrived, He Zhen was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Heluoai held the inner city while Qiaofang posted Chen De at the west gate and Deputy General Ren Zhen at the north gate; the two columns skirmished repeatedly until Li Guohan's relief force came up and He Zhen was routed.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，肅親王豪格師既入川，喬芳亦遣總兵官範蘇等攻獻忠部眾，為伏柷溪第溝子，戰白水、青川，屢破之；

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year, after Prince Su Hooge's army had entered Sichuan, Qiaofang also sent Regional Commander Fan Su and others to attack Zhang Xianzhong's followers, ambushing them at Zhudi Gouzi in Zhuxi, fighting at Baishui and Qingchuan, and repeatedly defeating them;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year, once Prince Su Hooge's forces were in Sichuan, Qiaofang too sent Regional Commander Fan Su and others against Zhang Xianzhong's remnants. They laid an ambush at Zhudi Gouzi in Zhuxi, fought at Baishui and Qingchuan, and won a series of victories;

sentences.zh: 復以反間殺其渠況益勤等，遂收龍安。

translations.literal: He further used counter-intelligence to kill their chieftains Kuang Yiqin and others, and thus recovered Long'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned disinformation against the rebel leaders, killing Kuang Yiqin and others, and recovered Long'an.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，喬芳帥師出駐固原，討大定之黨，分遣諸將任珍擊斬白天爵等；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, Qiaofang led his army out to encamp at Guyuan and suppress the faction of Wu Dading, dispatching the generals separately; Ren Zhen attacked and beheaded Bai Tianjue and others;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year Qiaofang marched out and made camp at Guyuan to crush Wu Dading's party. He sent his commanders in separate columns: Ren Zhen struck down and beheaded Bai Tianjue and others;

sentences.zh: 劉芳名攻寧夏，俘王元、焦浴；

translations.literal: Liu Fangming attacked Ningxia and captured Wang Yuan and Jiao Yu;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fangming attacked Ningxia and took Wang Yuan and Jiao Yu prisoner;

sentences.zh: 陳德攻鎮原，降姬蛟、王總管：於是固原西北悉定。

translations.literal: Chen De attacked Zhenyuan and received the surrender of Ji Jiao and Wang Zongguan: thus the northwest of Guyuan was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chen De attacked Zhenyuan and accepted the surrender of Ji Jiao and Wang Zongguan, and with that the northwest around Guyuan was fully secured.

sentences.zh: 復遣珍、德及副將馬寧、王平徇興安，討賀珍之黨，戰蕎麥山，再戰板橋，斬胡向宸；

translations.literal: He again sent Zhen, De, and Deputy Generals Ma Ning and Wang Ping to pacify Xing'an and suppress He Zhen's faction; they fought at Qiaomai Mountain, fought again at Banqiao, and beheaded Hu Xiangchen;
translations.idiomatic: Qiaofang next sent Ren Zhen, Chen De, and Deputy Generals Ma Ning and Wang Ping to sweep Xing'an and hunt down He Zhen's allies. They fought at Qiaomai Mountain, fought again at Banqiao, and beheaded Hu Xiangchen;

sentences.zh: 困椒溝，破藥箭寨，斬孫守法；

translations.literal: They trapped them at Jiaogou, broke Yaojian Stockade, and beheaded Sun Shoufa;
translations.idiomatic: They cornered the rebels at Jiaogou, stormed Yaojian Stockade, and beheaded Sun Shoufa;

sentences.zh: 破漫營山寨，擒米國軫、李世英：於是興安定。

translations.literal: They broke Manying Mountain Stockade and captured Mi Guozhen and Li Shiying: thus Xing'an was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They overran Manying Mountain Stockade and captured Mi Guozhen and Li Shiying, and Xing'an was brought under control.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，馬德亂寧夏，復遣馬寧會寧夏兵共討之。

translations.literal: That autumn Ma De stirred up trouble in Ningxia, and Qiaofang again sent Ma Ning to join with Ningxia troops in a joint campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Ma De rebelled in Ningxia, and Qiaofang once more dispatched Ma Ning to combine with local Ningxia forces and suppress him.

sentences.zh: 戰亂麻川，逐至河兒坪，斬德。

translations.literal: They fought at Luanma River, pursued him to He'er Ping, and beheaded De.
translations.idiomatic: At Luanma River they gave battle, chased him to He'er Ping, and killed Ma De.

sentences.zh: 又遣張勇、劉友元攻鐵角城，复戰安家川，擒賀宏器；

translations.literal: He also sent Zhang Yong and Liu Youyuan to attack Tie'ercheng, fought again at Anjia River, and captured He Hongqi;
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Zhang Yong and Liu Youyuan against Tie'ercheng, fought again at Anjia River, and took He Hongqi captive;

sentences.zh: 攻李明義寨，擒明義：於是環慶亦定。

translations.literal: They attacked Li Mingyi's stockade and captured Mingyi: thus Huanqing too was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They assaulted Li Mingyi's stockade and captured Mingyi himself, and Huanqing was secured as well.

sentences.zh: 乃益遣陳德、王平等招降青嘴寨渠折自明，三十六寨渠王希榮，轆轤寨渠高一祥，擊斬天峰寨渠張貴人，於是關中群盜垂盡。

translations.literal: He then further sent Chen De, Wang Ping, and others to receive the surrender of Qingzui Stockade chieftain Zhe Ziming, Thirty-Six Stockades chieftain Wang Xirong, and Lulu Stockade chieftain Gao Yixiang, and to attack and behead Tianfeng Stockade chieftain Zhang Guiren; thus the bandit hosts of Guanzhong were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaofang then sent Chen De, Wang Ping, and others to accept the submission of Zhe Ziming of Qingzui Stockade, Wang Xirong of the Thirty-Six Stockades, and Gao Yixiang of Lulu Stockade, while striking down Zhang Guiren, chieftain of Tianfeng Stockade. With that, the outlaw bands of Guanzhong were all but wiped out.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，流賊一朵雲、馬上飛等攻西鄉，喬芳遣任珍等討之，斬所署監軍許不惑，凡千餘級，生致其渠。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, the roving bandits Yiduo Yun, Mashangfei, and others attacked Xixiang; Qiaofang sent Ren Zhen and others to suppress them, beheaded the appointed supervising officer Xu Buhuo, more than a thousand in all in heads taken, and captured the chieftain alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year the bandit leaders Yiduo Yun and Mashangfei attacked Xixiang. Qiaofang sent Ren Zhen and others against them, killed their appointed military supervisor Xu Buhuo along with more than a thousand men, and took the ringleader alive.

sentences.zh: 河西回米喇印、丁國棟挾明延長王識駉為亂，既陷甘、涼，渡河東，殘岷、蘭、洮、河諸州，薄鞏昌。

translations.literal: The Hui of Hexi, Mi Layin and Ding Guodong, raised rebellion using the Ming Prince of Yanchang, Shi Ting, as their figurehead; having already taken Gan and Liang, they crossed east of the river and ravaged the prefectures of Min, Lan, Tao, and He, pressing close to Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Layin and Ding Guodong, Hui leaders west of the Yellow River, rebelled under the banner of the Ming Prince of Yanchang, Shi Ting. After seizing Ganzhou and Liangzhou they crossed to the east bank, laid waste to Minzhou, Lanzhou, Taozhou, and Hezhou, and advanced on Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 喬芳帥師出駐秦州，遣趙光瑞、馬寧等赴援，城兵出，夾擊，斬百餘級。

translations.literal: Qiaofang led his army out to encamp at Qinzhou and sent Zhao Guangrui, Ma Ning, and others to the relief; the garrison troops sallied forth, and in a pincer attack more than a hundred heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaofang marched out and encamped at Qinzhou, dispatching Zhao Guangrui, Ma Ning, and others to the rescue. The city garrison came out to meet them, and in a converging attack they cut down more than a hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 寧等復戰廣武坡，逐北七十餘裡，斬三千餘級，鞏昌圍解。

translations.literal: Ning and the others fought again at Guangwu Slope, pursued the enemy north for more than seventy li, took more than three thousand heads, and the siege of Gongchang was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ning's force fought again at Guangwu Slope, drove the rebels north for over seventy li, killed more than three thousand, and lifted the siege of Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 喇印、國棟之黨數百人，分擾臨洮、岷州內官營。

translations.literal: Several hundred followers of Layin and Guodong split up to harass Lin Tao and Neiguan Camp in Minzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred men from Layin and Guodong's party broke off to raid Lin Tao and Neiguan Camp in Minzhou.

sentences.zh: 喬芳部勒諸將，令張勇、陳萬略向臨洮，馬寧、劉友元取內官營，趙光瑞、佟透徇岷、洮、河三州。

translations.literal: Qiaofang arrayed his generals and ordered Zhang Yong and Chen Wanlue toward Lin Tao, Ma Ning and Liu Youyuan to take Neiguan Camp, and Zhao Guangrui and Tong Tou to pacify the three prefectures of Min, Tao, and He.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaofang deployed his commanders: Zhang Yong and Chen Wanlue were sent toward Lin Tao, Ma Ning and Liu Youyuan to seize Neiguan Camp, and Zhao Guangrui and Tong Tou to sweep Minzhou, Taozhou, and Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 勇等敗賊馬韓山，斬級七百，進复臨洮。

translations.literal: Yong and the others defeated the bandits at Mahan Mountain, took seven hundred heads, and advanced to recover Lin Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong's column routed the rebels at Mahan Mountain, killed seven hundred, and pushed on to retake Lin Tao.

sentences.zh: 光瑞等敗賊梅嶺，得其渠丁光射，斬級三千。

translations.literal: Guangrui and the others defeated the bandits at Meiling, captured their chieftain Ding Guangshe, and took three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guangrui's force defeated the rebels at Meiling, captured their leader Ding Guangshe, and killed three thousand.

sentences.zh: 岷、洮、河三州皆下。

translations.literal: The three prefectures of Min, Tao, and He all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhou, Taozhou, and Hezhou all submitted.

sentences.zh: 寧等直擊內官營，斬級八百。

translations.literal: Ning and the others struck Neiguan Camp directly and took eight hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ning's troops hit Neiguan Camp head-on and killed eight hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 喇印、國棟之徒退據蘭州。

translations.literal: The followers of Layin and Guodong withdrew and held Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Layin and Guodong's men fell back and fortified themselves in Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 閏四月，喬芳與侍郎額塞率師自鞏昌薄蘭州。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month, Qiaofang together with Vice Minister Esai led their army from Gongchang to press close to Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month Qiaofang and Vice Minister Esai marched from Gongchang and closed on Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 勇敗賊馬家坪，獲識駉，與寧、光瑞會師蘭州城下，攻拔之。

translations.literal: Yong defeated the bandits at Majia Ping, captured Shi Ting, joined forces with Ning and Guangrui below Lanzhou city, and stormed and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong routed the rebels at Majia Ping and captured Shi Ting, then united with Ma Ning and Zhao Guangrui beneath the walls of Lanzhou and took the city by assault.

sentences.zh: 別遣光瑞克舊洮州，其渠丁嘉升走死，師渡河。

translations.literal: Separately he sent Guangrui to capture Old Taozhou; its chieftain Ding Jiasheng fled and died, and the army crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhao Guangrui in another column to seize Old Taozhou, where the rebel leader Ding Jiasheng fled to his death; the main force then crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 七月，定涼州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Liangzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Liangzhou was secured.

sentences.zh: 八月，攻甘州，喬芳遣張勇夜攻城，而與昂邦章京傅喀禪及寧、光瑞等為繼。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they attacked Ganzhou; Qiaofang sent Zhang Yong to assault the city by night, while he himself with Angbang Zhangjing Fukeshan and Ning, Guangrui, and others followed in support.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they moved against Ganzhou. Qiaofang had Zhang Yong storm the walls by night, while he followed with Angbang Zhangjing Fukeshan, Ma Ning, Zhao Guangrui, and the rest as reserve.

sentences.zh: 喇印等食盡，皆出降。

translations.literal: Layin and the others exhausted their provisions and all came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Layin and his men ran out of food, they all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 六年，徵諸道兵下四川。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, troops from all routes were summoned to descend on Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year forces from every district were mobilized for the campaign into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 喇印降後授副將，在蘭州軍中，覘鎮兵憚遠征，因惎中軍參將蔣國泰，戕甘肅巡撫張文衡等，據甘州以叛。

translations.literal: After Layin surrendered he was appointed deputy general and remained with the army at Lanzhou; observing that the garrison troops feared a distant expedition, he incited Middle Army Assistant Commander Jiang Guotai, killed Gansu Governor Zhang Wenheng and others, and seized Ganzhou in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: After his surrender Layin was made deputy general and kept with the Lanzhou garrison. Seeing that the local troops dreaded a long march, he turned Middle Army Assistant Commander Jiang Guotai against the Qing, murdered Gansu Governor Zhang Wenheng and others, and rebelled from Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 國棟亦攻陷涼、肅二州。

translations.literal: Guodong also attacked and took the two prefectures of Liang and Su.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Guodong likewise captured Liangzhou and Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 喬芳帥師自蘭州渡河而西，與傅喀禪等會師合圍，攻不下，深溝堅壘以困之。

translations.literal: Qiaofang led his army from Lanzhou, crossed the river westward, joined Fukeshan and the others in a united encirclement, and though they could not take the city by assault, they dug deep trenches and built strong stockades to starve the defenders.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaofang marched from Lanzhou, crossed west of the river, and combined with Fukeshan to ring the rebels. Unable to storm the city, he entangled them with deep trenches and fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 喇印等食盡夜遁，喬芳遣兵追及之水泉，擊殺喇印。

translations.literal: Layin and the others, their provisions exhausted, fled by night; Qiaofang sent troops in pursuit, caught up with them at Shuiquan, and killed Layin in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Layin and his men ran out of food they broke out by night. Qiaofang's pursuers overtook them at Shuiquan and killed Layin.

sentences.zh: 國棟復與纏頭回土倫泰等據肅州，號倫泰王，而國棟自署總兵官，城守，出掠武威、張掖、酒泉。

translations.literal: Guodong again joined with the Chantou Hui Tuluntai and others to hold Suzhou, styled Tuluntai king, while Guodong himself appointed himself regional commander, defended the city, and sallied forth to plunder Wuwei, Zhangye, and Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Guodong then joined the Chantou Hui leader Tuluntai in holding Suzhou, where Tuluntai proclaimed himself king while Guodong styled himself regional commander, held the walls, and raided Wuwei, Zhangye, and Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 會平陽盜渠虞允、韓昭宣等應大同叛將薑瓖為亂，以三十萬人陷蒲州，上命喬芳與額塞還軍御之。

translations.literal: Just then the Pingyang bandit chieftains Yu Yun, Han Zhaoxuan, and others responded to the Datong rebel general Jiang Xiang in rebellion, and with three hundred thousand men took Puzhou; the Emperor ordered Qiaofang and Esai to return their armies to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the Pingyang outlaw leaders Yu Yun and Han Zhaoxuan rallied to the Datong mutineer Jiang Xiang, and with three hundred thousand men seized Puzhou. The throne ordered Qiaofang and Esai to turn back and confront them.

sentences.zh: 喬芳留勇、寧等圍肅州，率師遂東。

translations.literal: Qiaofang left Yong, Ning, and others to besiege Suzhou and led his army eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaofang left Zhang Yong, Ma Ning, and others to continue the siege of Suzhou and marched east himself.

sentences.zh: 八月，師自潼關濟，督協領根特、副將趙光瑞等克蒲州，斬級七千。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the army crossed at Tong Pass; supervising Assistant Commander Gent, Deputy General Zhao Guangrui, and others took Puzhou and took seven thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month his force crossed at Tong Pass. Under his direction Assistant Commander Gent, Deputy General Zhao Guangrui, and others captured Puzhou and killed seven thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 進次寧晉，瓖將白璋等六千人往攻榮河，光瑞等擊破之，斬級二千有奇。

translations.literal: Advancing he halted at Ningjin; Xiang's general Bai Zhang and six thousand others went to attack Ronghe, and Guangrui and the others defeated them and took more than two thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: The army pushed on to Ningjin. Jiang Xiang's general Bai Zhang marched six thousand men against Ronghe, but Zhao Guangrui's force broke them and killed more than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 璋北走，師從之，迫河，賊多入水死，遂擊斬璋。

translations.literal: Zhang fled north; the army followed him, pressed him to the river, many bandits entered the water and died, and they then attacked and beheaded Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zhang fled north; Qiaofang's troops pursued him to the river, where many rebels drowned, and then cut Zhang down.

sentences.zh: 餘賊入孫吉鎮，殲焉。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits entered Sunji Town and were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors withdrew into Sunji Town and were wiped out there.

sentences.zh: 復進向猗氏，行十餘裡，瓖所置監軍道衛登方以數千人依山拒我師，其將張萬全又以四千人助戰。

translations.literal: They again advanced toward Yishi; after marching more than ten li, the supervising officer Jiang Xiang had appointed, Dao Wei Dengfang, with several thousand men took the hills to resist our army, and his general Zhang Wanquan brought another four thousand to assist in the fight.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced again on Yishi. After a march of more than ten li they met Dao Wei Dengfang, the military supervisor Jiang Xiang had installed, holding the hills with several thousand men, while his general Zhang Wanquan brought four thousand more to the fight.

sentences.zh: 光瑞等擊斬萬全，乃還攻，獲登方，斬其將王國賢等三十餘人、級三千有奇。

translations.literal: Guangrui and the others attacked and beheaded Wanquan, then turned back to the assault, captured Dengfang, and beheaded his generals Wang Guoxian and more than thirty others, with more than three thousand heads in all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guangrui's men killed Zhang Wanquan, wheeled about for the assault, took Dao Wei Dengfang prisoner, and beheaded more than thirty of his officers including Wang Guoxian, killing more than three thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 又令章京杜敏等攻解州，破其渠邊王張五、黨自成等。

translations.literal: He also ordered Zhangjing Du Min and others to attack Jiezhou and defeat its chieftains Bianwang Zhang Wu, Dang Zicheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Zhangjing Du Min and others against Jiezhou, where they broke the rebel leaders Bianwang Zhang Wu, Dang Zicheng, and their followers.

sentences.zh: 榮河、猗氏、解州皆下。

translations.literal: Ronghe, Yishi, and Jiezhou all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Ronghe, Yishi, and Jiezhou all came under Qing control.

sentences.zh: 杜敏等殲餘寇。

translations.literal: Du Min and the others annihilated the remaining bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Du Min's force mopped up the last of the rebels.

sentences.zh: 根特等又破所置都督郭中傑於侯馬驛。

translations.literal: Gent and the others again defeated the installed regional commander Guo Zhongjie at Houma Post.
translations.idiomatic: Gent's column routed the rebel-appointed commander Guo Zhongjie at Houma Post.

sentences.zh: 九月，光瑞等進克運城，斬允、昭宣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Guangrui and the others advanced and took Yuncheng, beheading Yun and Zhaoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zhao Guangrui's force pushed into Yuncheng and executed Yu Yun and Han Zhaoxuan.

sentences.zh: 瓖之徒內犯者皆盡誅。

translations.literal: All of Xiang's followers who had raided inward were entirely put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Every one of Jiang Xiang's men who had struck inland was hunted down and killed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，勇、寧克肅州，誅國棟、倫泰及其黨黑承印等，斬五千餘級。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yong and Ning took Suzhou, executed Guodong, Tuluntai, and their partisan Hei Chengyin and others, and took more than five thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhang Yong and Ma Ning captured Suzhou, put Ding Guodong, Tuluntai, and their lieutenant Hei Chengyin to death, and killed more than five thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 河西平。

translations.literal: The Hexi region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The west of the river was at last quiet.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，論功，加兵部尚書，進世職一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year, merit was assessed; he was promoted to Minister of War and advanced one grade in his hereditary adaha hafan rank.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were tallied in the third month of the seventh year, he was made Minister of War and his hereditary adaha hafan was raised one grade.

sentences.zh: 十二月，喬芳遣任珍擊斬興安寇何可亮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Qiaofang sent Ren Zhen to attack and behead the Xing'an bandit He Keiliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Qiaofang dispatched Ren Zhen, who hunted down and killed the Xing'an outlaw He Keiliang.

sentences.zh: 是年，遣趙光瑞等討北山寇劉宏才，戰保安，擒其軍師苗惠民；

translations.literal: That year he dispatched Zhao Guangrui and others to suppress the Beishan bandit Liu Hongcai; at Bao'an they fought and captured his strategist Miao Huimin;
translations.idiomatic: The same year he sent Zhao Guangrui against the Beishan rebel Liu Hongcai; at Bao'an they routed his force and took his strategist Miao Huimin prisoner;

sentences.zh: 戰合水，擒斬宏才。

translations.literal: At Heshui they fought, captured and beheaded Hongcai.
translations.idiomatic: at Heshui they caught Liu Hongcai and executed him.

sentences.zh: 八年，遣游擊陳明順等擊敗雒南寇何柴山，游擊仰九明诇紫陽山寇孫守全；

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he sent battalion commander Chen Mingshun and others to defeat the Luonan bandit He Chaishan, and battalion commander Yang Jiuming to reconnoiter the Ziyang Mountain bandit Sun Shouquan;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he ordered the battalion commander Chen Mingshun to break the Luonan rebel He Chaishan, and sent Yang Jiuming to scout the Ziyang Mountain chieftain Sun Shouquan;

sentences.zh: 復令光瑞等會興安鎮兵擊斬守全及其徒翹興寧、趙定國、謝天奇等，犁其寨。

translations.literal: He again ordered Guangrui and the others to join Xing'an garrison troops, attack and behead Shouquan and his followers Qiao Xingning, Zhao Dingguo, Xie Tianqi, and others, and raze their stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Guangrui join the Xing'an garrison, cut down Sun Shouquan and his lieutenants Qiao Xingning, Zhao Dingguo, and Xie Tianqi, and level their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 喬芳督陝西十年，破滅群盜，降其脅從，前後十七萬六千有奇。

translations.literal: Qiaofang governed Shaanxi for ten years, destroyed and extinguished the bandit hosts, and received the surrender of their coerced followers—altogether more than one hundred seventy-six thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: In ten years as governor of Shaanxi, Qiaofang broke the rebel armies and brought in more than 176,000 men who had followed them under duress.

sentences.zh: 獎拔諸將，不限資格，如張勇、馬寧、趙光瑞、陳德、狄應魁、劉友元輩，皆自偏裨至專閫。

translations.literal: He rewarded and promoted generals without limiting by qualifications; men such as Zhang Yong, Ma Ning, Zhao Guangrui, Chen De, Di Yingkui, and Liu Youyuan all rose from minor officers to independent regional command.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted on merit rather than pedigree: Zhang Yong, Ma Ning, Zhao Guangrui, Chen De, Di Yingkui, Liu Youyuan, and others all climbed from junior ranks to full regional command.

sentences.zh: 諸寇既殄，疏言：「陝西寇劇，多荒田，請蠲其賦。

translations.literal: Once the bandits were exterminated, he submitted a memorial saying: "Shaanxi suffered severely from bandits and has much wasteland; I request remission of its taxes.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were gone he memorialized the throne: "Banditry has ravaged Shaanxi and left much land fallow. I ask that its taxes be remitted.

sentences.zh: 分兵徠民，行屯田法。

translations.literal: Dispense troops to summon the people back and implement the garrison-farming system.
translations.idiomatic: Send out troops to recall the people and put the garrison-colony system in place.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣諸將白士麟等分屯延慶、平固諸地，歲得粟四​​萬二千石有奇，以佐軍糈。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched the generals Bai Shilin and others to garrison separately at Yanqing, Pinggu, and other places; each year they obtained more than forty-two thousand shi of grain to supplement army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He then posted Bai Shilin and other commanders to farm colonies around Yanqing, Pinggu, and elsewhere, yielding more than 42,000 shi of grain a year to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 恩詔累進三等阿思哈尼哈番，加太子太保。

translations.literal: By imperial grace he was repeatedly promoted to third-class ashan i hafan and made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favor raised him step by step to third-class ashan i hafan and Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，命兼督四川兵馬錢糧，疏言：「陝西七鎮及督撫各標為兵九萬八千有奇，合滿洲四旗及平西王吳三桂、固山額真李國翰兩軍，歲餉三百六十萬而弱，而陝西賦入一百八十六萬，不足者殆半，後將難繼。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year he was ordered also to supervise Sichuan's troops, horses, funds, and grain, and submitted a memorial saying: "Shaanxi's seven garrisons together with the various banners of the governor-general and grand coordinators total more than ninety-eight thousand troops; combined with the four Manchu banners and the two armies of the Prince of the West Wu Sangui and the gushen ejen Li Guohan, yearly pay exceeds three million six hundred thousand, while Shaanxi's tax revenue is one million eight hundred sixty thousand—the shortfall is nearly half, and sustaining this later will be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the tenth year he was told to oversee Sichuan's troops, horses, funds, and grain as well, and wrote: "Shaanxi's seven garrisons and the banners under the governor-general and grand coordinators field more than 98,000 men. Add the four Manchu banners plus the armies of the Prince of the West Wu Sangui and the gushen ejen Li Guohan, and annual pay runs to more than 3.6 million taels—yet Shaanxi collects only 1.86 million. Nearly half must come from elsewhere, and that cannot last.

sentences.zh: 甘肅處邊遠興安界，三省兵當循舊額。

translations.literal: Gansu lies on the remote border at Xing'an; the three provinces' troops should follow the old quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu sits on a distant frontier beside Xing'an; the armies of all three provinces should keep their old establishments.

sentences.zh: 延綏、寧夏、固原、臨鞏四鎮鎮留三千人，慶陽協五百人，餘五千五百人可省也。

translations.literal: At the four garrisons of Yansui, Ningxia, Guyuan, and Linggong retain three thousand men; at the Qingyang detachment five hundred; the remaining five thousand five hundred can be cut.
translations.idiomatic: At Yansui, Ningxia, Guyuan, and Linggong keep 3,000 men; at Qingyang 500; the other 5,500 can go.

sentences.zh: 漢羌既駐三桂、國翰兩軍，宜裁總兵官。

translations.literal: Since Hanzhong and the Qiang region already station the two armies of Sangui and Guohan, the post of regional commander should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong and the Qiang frontier already hold Sangui's and Guohan's two armies—the regional commander there should be removed.

sentences.zh: 興鎮置副，留千人，陽平關、黑水峪、漢陰縣各五百人，餘二千五百人可省也。

translations.literal: At the Xing'an garrison place a deputy, retain one thousand men; at Yangping Pass, Heishui Valley, and Hanyin County five hundred each; the remaining two thousand five hundred can be cut.
translations.idiomatic: Leave a deputy at Xing'an with 1,000 men; 500 each at Yangping Pass, Heishui Valley, and Hanyin County; 2,500 more can be cut.

sentences.zh: 提督駐省會，留二千人，餘二千人亦可省也。

translations.literal: The governor-general stationed at the provincial capital retains two thousand; the other two thousand can also be cut.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general at the provincial seat needs 2,000; the other 2,000 can be cut as well.

sentences.zh: 各道標兵悉令屯田，延鎮、定邊、神木三道無屯田，止用守兵，計所省又二千餘人。

translations.literal: All circuit banner troops are to be ordered to farm garrison lands; the Yansui, Dingbian, and Shenmu circuits have no garrison farms and use only garrison troops—a further saving of more than two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Every circuit banner should farm; Yansui, Dingbian, and Shenmu, which cannot farm, need only garrison guards—another 2,000 men saved.

sentences.zh: 都省兵一萬二千人，省餉歲三十一萬。

translations.literal: Altogether from the province twelve thousand troops can be cut, saving three hundred ten thousand in yearly pay.
translations.idiomatic: In all, 12,000 men can be struck from the provincial rolls, saving 310,000 taels a year.

sentences.zh: 今四川未定，當令右路總兵官馬寧率精兵三千駐保寧，以步兵五千分駐保寧迤北廣元、昭化間，以屯田為持久。

translations.literal: Now Sichuan is not yet settled; the Right Route regional commander Ma Ning should be ordered to lead three thousand picked troops to garrison Baoning, with five thousand foot soldiers distributed north of Baoning between Guangyuan and Zhaohua, making garrison farming the basis for a sustained campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan is still unsettled. Ma Ning, regional commander of the Right Route, should take 3,000 elite troops to Baoning and station 5,000 foot soldiers north of it between Guangyuan and Zhaohua, using garrison colonies to sustain a long campaign.

sentences.zh: 三桂駐漢中，相為犄角，規取四川。

translations.literal: Sangui garrisons at Hanzhong, the two forming pincers, to plan the seizure of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui holds Hanzhong; the two wings can pinch Sichuan and take it.

sentences.zh: 」既，复疏言：「師進取四川，宜隨在留兵駐防，以樹干城，謀生聚。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again submitted a memorial saying: "As the army advances to take Sichuan, troops should be left wherever it passes to garrison and defend, to plant trunks of fortress-cities and plan for population growth and accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: He followed with another memorial: "As the army moves into Sichuan, leave troops at every point taken to hold the ground, build strongpoints, and restore people and grain.

sentences.zh: 師行，當人給馬三、伴丁一，攜甲仗，以利攸往。

translations.literal: When the army marches, each man should be given three horses and one attendant, carrying armor and weapons, to facilitate rapid movement wherever needed.
translations.idiomatic: On the march, give each soldier three horses, one servant, and full arms so he can go wherever the campaign demands.

sentences.zh: 」上褒其謀當。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his plan as sound.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 十月，西寧回謀為亂，遣狄應魁捕治，得其渠祁敖、牙固子等以歸。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Xining Muslims plotted rebellion; he dispatched Di Yingkui to capture and punish them, and brought back their ringleaders Qi Ao, Yaguzi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Muslims at Xining plotted revolt; he sent Di Yingkui to suppress them and returned with the ringleaders Qi Ao, Yaguzi, and their fellows.

sentences.zh: 喬芳屢乞退，至是以疾告，加少保，召還京師。

translations.literal: Qiaofang had repeatedly begged to retire; now he reported illness, was made Junior Guardian, and summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaofang had long asked to step down; now, pleading illness, he was made Junior Guardian and recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十二月，命未至而喬芳卒，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, before the order arrived Qiaofang died; he was posthumously titled Zhongyi ("Loyal and Resolute").
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, before the summons reached him, Qiaofang died; the court gave him the posthumous name Zhongyi, Loyal and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 太宗拔用諸降將，從入關，出領方面，喬芳績最顯，張存仁亞焉。

translations.literal: Taizong selected and employed various surrendered generals who followed him through the pass and went out to govern regions; Qiaofang's achievements were the most outstanding, with Zhang Cunren next.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji had plucked surrendered generals from the ranks, brought them through the pass, and sent them to govern the provinces; among them Qiaofang shone brightest, with Zhang Cunren close behind.

sentences.zh: 聖祖嘗誡漢軍諸官吏，因曰：「祖宗定鼎初，委任漢軍諸官吏，與滿洲一體。

translations.literal: The Shengzu once admonished the Han Banner officials, saying: "At the founding when the ancestors established the dynasty, they entrusted Han Banner officials, treating them the same as Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor once warned Han Banner officials: "When our forefathers founded the dynasty, they entrusted Han Banner men and treated them as equals of the Manchus.

sentences.zh: 其間頗有宣猷效力如喬芳、存仁輩，朝廷亦得其用」云。

translations.literal: Among them some indeed proclaimed their counsels and served with effect, like Qiaofang, Cunren, and their ilk; the court also gained their use," he said.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were men who offered sound counsel and served well—Qiaofang, Cunren, and others like them—and the court put them to good use," he said.

sentences.zh: 張文衡，遼東開平衛人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenheng was a native of Kaipingwei in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenheng came from Kaipingwei in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 明諸生。

translations.literal: A Ming licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the Ming licentiate examination.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年閏八月，太宗自將伐明，入宣府。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month of Tiancong 8, Taizong personally led a campaign against the Ming and entered Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month of Tiancong 8, Hong Taiji led the army against the Ming in person and marched into Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 文衡自大同詣軍前求見，言在明為代王參謀。

translations.literal: Wenheng came from Datong to the army camp to request an audience, saying that under the Ming he had been strategic adviser to the Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wenheng walked from Datong to the camp and asked to be received, explaining that he had served the Ming as strategist to the Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 明諸臣方尚貪酷，虐民罔上，必有聖主應天而興，故徒步上謁。

translations.literal: Ming officials at the time prized greed and cruelty, abused the people and deceived their superiors; a sage ruler must rise in response to Heaven—so he came on foot to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: Ming ministers then worshipped greed and cruelty, grinding the people and lying to the throne; a sage king must rise to answer Heaven—and so he had come on foot to offer himself.

sentences.zh: 旋疏言：「大同城小而堅，師攻當先關而后城，攻關宜穴地。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted a memorial saying: "Datong's walls are small but strong; in attacking, the army should take the passes first and then the city; in attacking passes, tunneling is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: He soon wrote: "Datong is small but stout. Take the passes before the city; to storm a pass, dig under the walls.

sentences.zh: 宣府城大破碎，宜決洋河灌之。

translations.literal: Xuanfu's walls are large but broken; the Yang River should be breached to flood it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanfu is vast but crumbling—break the Yang River and flood it."

sentences.zh: 」九年正月，复疏策進取，言：「明文武將吏皆以賂得，無謀無勇；

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he again submitted a strategy for advance, saying: "Ming civil and military officers and officials all obtained their posts through bribery—they have neither counsel nor courage;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year he submitted another plan of conquest: "Ming civil and military officers buy their posts—they have no strategy and no nerve;

sentences.zh: 又以貪故，餉減器窳，兵不用命。

translations.literal: and because of greed, pay is reduced and weapons are shoddy, so the troops do not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: greed has pared their pay and left their arms worthless, so the soldiers will not fight as ordered.

sentences.zh: 所以能拒我者，不過畏殺、畏掠、畏父母妻子離散，乃倚火器以死禦我。

translations.literal: The reason they can resist us is only that they fear slaughter, fear plunder, fear separation from parents, wives, and children—thus they rely on firearms to defend unto death against us.
translations.idiomatic: They resist only because they dread slaughter, looting, and the scattering of their families—so they cling to gunpowder weapons and sell their lives dearly.

sentences.zh: 今宣、大新被兵，山、陝、川、湖陷於流賊。

translations.literal: Now Xuanfu and Datong have newly suffered warfare; Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Huguang have fallen to roving bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanfu and Datong have just been ravaged; Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Huguang are overrun by roving rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊半天下，兵亦半天下。

translations.literal: Bandits hold half the realm, and armies too occupy half the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels hold half the empire—and armies consume the other half.

sentences.zh: 惟東南無事，又困於新餉。

translations.literal: Only the southeast is undisturbed, yet it is also strained by the new land tax.
translations.idiomatic: Only the southeast is still at peace, and even there the new levy is crushing the people.

sentences.zh: 上不及此時進兵，明不恆弱，我不恆強，節短勢險，人有鼎立之志。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, if you do not advance troops at this moment, the Ming will not always be weak nor we always strong; resources are limited and the situation perilous, and men will harbor the will to stand as three rival powers.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not strike now, Ming weakness and our strength will not last; means are short and the ground treacherous, and men will begin to dream of three kingdoms standing apart.

sentences.zh: 豈非自失其機，反貽異日憂乎？

translations.literal: Would this not be losing one's opportunity and instead bequeathing worry for another day?
translations.idiomatic: Would that not mean squandering the moment and storing up trouble for years to come?

sentences.zh: 原上毋負天生上之心也。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty not to fall short of what Heaven intended in raising you.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will not betray the purpose for which Heaven set you on the throne.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上曰：「待朕思之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor said, "Let me consider it."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne, and the Emperor replied, "Leave it to me—I will think it over."

sentences.zh: 」二月，遣貝勒多爾袞帥師收察哈爾。

translations.literal: In the second month, Prince Dorgon was dispatched at the head of an army to bring Chahar to submission.
translations.idiomatic: That second month, Prince Dorgon was sent at the head of an army to subdue Chahar.

sentences.zh: 文衡又言：「宜率蒙古入偏岢，略太原，假中國物力以富蒙古；

translations.literal: Wenheng further urged: "You should lead the Mongols through Pianguan Pass, raid Taiyuan, and borrow the material strength of China to enrich Mongolia;
translations.idiomatic: Wenheng pressed the point again: "Lead the Mongols through Pianguan Pass, strike at Taiyuan, and use the resources of China to enrich Mongolia;

sentences.zh: 且張軍威，並可近招流賊，並力並進。

translations.literal: Moreover you can display military might, and at the same time summon roving bandits from nearby, joining forces to advance together."
translations.idiomatic: display your armies' power, and at the same time draw in the roving rebels close at hand—unite your strength and press forward as one."

sentences.zh: 」上授文衡秘書院副理事官，賜田宅、銀幣，以大臣雅希禪女妻焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Wenheng deputy director of the Secretariat, granted him fields, a residence, and silver, and gave him in marriage the daughter of the minister Yaxi Chan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Wenheng deputy director of the Secretariat, rewarded him with land, a house, and silver, and gave him the daughter of the minister Yaxi Chan as his wife.

sentences.zh: 隸鑲黃旗漢軍。

translations.literal: He was placed under the Chinese Eight Banners of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was registered with the Chinese Eight Banners of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，出為山東青州知府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, he was sent out as prefect of Qingzhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi, he was appointed prefect of Qingzhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 初上官，總兵官柯永盛以戍青州之兵徇高密，而侍郎王鰲永以招撫至，主餉。

translations.literal: Shortly after he took office, the regional commander Ke Yongsheng led the Qingzhou garrison on a pacification campaign in Gaomi, while Vice Minister Wang Aoyong arrived on a mission of recruitment and pacification and was put in charge of supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he assumed his post, Regional Commander Ke Yongsheng marched the Qingzhou garrison to pacify Gaomi, while Vice Minister Wang Aoyong arrived on a conciliation mission and took charge of provisions.

sentences.zh: 趙應元者，從李自成為旗鼓，覸青州兵寡，陽就鰲永降，請置孥於城。

translations.literal: One Zhao Yingyuan had served Li Zicheng as a flag-and-drum officer; seeing that Qingzhou's forces were few, he feigned submission to Aoyong and asked to quarter his wife and children in the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yingyuan had once served Li Zicheng as a standard-bearer; noting how thin Qingzhou's defenses were, he pretended to surrender to Aoyong and asked leave to settle his family inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 既入，遂執殺鰲永。

translations.literal: Once inside, he seized and killed Aoyong.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was within the city, he seized Aoyong and killed him.

sentences.zh: 文衡見應元，為好語，具疏請留鎮。

translations.literal: Wenheng met Yingyuan, spoke kindly to him, and submitted a detailed memorial requesting that he be left to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: Wenheng went to see Yingyuan, treated him with courtesy, and memorialized the throne asking that he be allowed to remain and hold the city.

sentences.zh: 應元喜，攫庫金，群酗。

translations.literal: Yingyuan was delighted; he seized treasury silver and his men drank together in revelry.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyuan was overjoyed. He plundered the treasury and his men caroused together.

sentences.zh: 會梅勒額真和託、李率泰率禁旅略登、萊，道青州，營城西北。

translations.literal: Just then the meile ejen Hetuo and Li Shuaitai, leading the imperial guards on a campaign across Dengzhou and Laizhou, passed through Qingzhou and encamped northwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the meile ejen Hetuo and Li Shuaitai, commanding the imperial guard on a sweep through Dengzhou and Laizhou, came by way of Qingzhou and made camp northwest of the city.

sentences.zh: 文衡惎應元出謁和託等，慰勞遣還，密令兵從入，夜起戮應元及其黨數十人。

translations.literal: Wenheng incited Yingyuan to go out and pay his respects to Hetuo and the others; after offering civilities he sent him back, but secretly ordered troops to follow him in. That night they rose and slaughtered Yingyuan and several dozen of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Wenheng goaded Yingyuan into going out to pay his respects to Hetuo and his officers; after receiving him with courtesy and sending him back, he secretly ordered soldiers to slip in after him. That night they rose up and cut down Yingyuan and several dozen of his men.

sentences.zh: 青州平。

translations.literal: Qingzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou was restored to order.

sentences.zh: 二年，移淮安府知府。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to be prefect of Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was moved to the prefecture of Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 豫親王多鐸下揚州，道淮安。

translations.literal: Prince Dodo of Yu, marching on Yangzhou, passed through Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dodo of Yu, on his descent toward Yangzhou, passed through Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 文衡請禁將吏毋擾市，糗糧芻秣應期立辦。

translations.literal: Wenheng petitioned that officers and clerks be forbidden to disturb the markets, and that rations of grain and fodder be prepared on schedule without delay.
translations.idiomatic: Wenheng petitioned that officers and staff be forbidden to harass the markets, and that grain and fodder be readied on time.

sentences.zh: 三遷，巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: After three further promotions, he became grand coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted three times in succession, he was made grand coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 五年二月上官，踰月而遘米喇印之亂。

translations.literal: He assumed that post in the second month of the fifth year; within a month he met the rebellion of Mi Layin.
translations.idiomatic: He took up the post in the second month of the fifth year, and within a month the rebellion of Mi Layin broke upon him.

sentences.zh: 變未作，喇印詭言要文衡造其家集議。

translations.literal: Before the uprising broke out, Layin sent word under false pretences that he wanted Wenheng to come to his home for a joint consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Before the revolt erupted, Layin sent a deceptive summons asking Wenheng to come to his house for a council.

sentences.zh: 文衡行未至，賊環射殺之。

translations.literal: Wenheng had not yet arrived when the rebels surrounded him and shot him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wenheng had not yet reached the place when the rebels closed in around him and shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 總兵劉良臣，副將毛鑌、潘雲騰，游擊黃得成、金印，都司王之俊，守備胡大年、李廷試、李承澤、陳九功皆死。

translations.literal: Regional commander Liu Liangchen, vice commanders Mao Bin and Pan Yunteng, battalion commanders Huang Decheng and Jin Yin, division director Wang Zhijun, and garrison commanders Hu Danian, Li Tingshi, Li Chengze, and Chen Jiugong all died.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Liu Liangchen, Vice Commanders Mao Bin and Pan Yunteng, Battalion Commanders Huang Decheng and Jin Yin, Division Director Wang Zhijun, and Garrison Commanders Hu Danian, Li Tingshi, Li Chengze, and Chen Jiugong all perished.

sentences.zh: 參將翟大有與戰，沒於陣。

translations.literal: Assistant commander Zhai Dayou fought and fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commander Zhai Dayou fought and died on the field.

sentences.zh: 賊挾西寧道副使林維造至北關，扌益殺之。

translations.literal: The rebels took Lin Weizao, vice commissioner of the Xining circuit, to the North Gate and beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dragged Lin Weizao, vice commissioner of the Xining circuit, to the North Gate and killed him by beating.

sentences.zh: 越日，陷涼州，戕西寧道參議張鵬翼。

translations.literal: The next day they took Liangzhou and killed Zhang Pengyi, assistant administration commissioner of the Xining circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The following day they seized Liangzhou and murdered Zhang Pengyi, assistant administration commissioner of the Xining circuit.

sentences.zh: 賊四出侵掠，破鞏昌，戕臨鞏兵備道李絮飛；

translations.literal: The rebels ranged in all directions raiding and plundering; they took Gongchang and killed Li Xufei, regional military intendant of Lin'gong;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fanned out in every direction, looting as they went. They overran Gongchang and killed Li Xufei, the Lin'gong military intendant;

sentences.zh: 破岷州，戕知州杜懋哲、王札；

translations.literal: took Minzhou and killed prefects Du Maozhe and Wang Zha;
translations.idiomatic: overran Minzhou and killed Prefects Du Maozhe and Wang Zha;

sentences.zh: 破蘭州，戕同知趙衝學，知​​州趙翀，訓導白旗、國學錦；

translations.literal: took Lanzhou and killed vice prefect Zhao Chongxue, prefect Zhao Chong, and instructors Bai Qi and Guo Xuejin;
translations.idiomatic: overran Lanzhou and killed Vice Prefect Zhao Chongxue, Prefect Zhao Chong, and Instructors Bai Qi and Guo Xuejin;

sentences.zh: 破臨洮，戕同知徐養奇；

translations.literal: took Lintao and killed vice prefect Xu Yangqi;
translations.idiomatic: overran Lintao and killed Vice Prefect Xu Yangqi;

sentences.zh: 破渭源，戕知縣李淐；

translations.literal: took Weiyuan and killed county magistrate Li Cheng;
translations.idiomatic: overran Weiyuan and killed County Magistrate Li Cheng;

sentences.zh: 戰通渭，圍子山，知縣周盛時被創死。

translations.literal: At a battle in Tongwei at Weizishan, County Magistrate Zhou Shengshi was wounded and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongwei, on Weizishan, County Magistrate Zhou Shengshi was wounded in battle and died.

sentences.zh: 事平，皆贈卹如例。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, all were posthumously honored and compensated according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, all received posthumous honors and pensions according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 張存仁，遼陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Cunren was a native of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cunren came from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 明寧遠副將，與總兵祖大壽同守大凌河。

translations.literal: A vice commander at Ningyuan under the Ming, he held Daling River together with Regional Commander Zu Dashou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming he had been vice commander at Ningyuan and, together with Regional Commander Zu Dashou, defended Daling River.

sentences.zh: 天聰五年，太宗自將攻大凌河，從大壽出降，仍授副將。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiancong, when the Taizong personally led an attack on Daling River, he followed Dashou in surrendering and was still granted the rank of vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tiancong, when the Taizong led the assault on Daling River in person, he followed Dashou in surrender and was again given the rank of vice commander.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，存仁與副將張洪謨、參將高光輝、游擊方獻可合疏請乘時進取，參將薑新別疏請令副將祖可法、劉天祿先取松、杏二城，則錦州自下。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, Cunren together with Vice Commanders Zhang Hongmo, Assistant Commander Gao Guanghui, and Battalion Commander Fang Xiank submitted a joint memorial urging a timely advance; Assistant Commander Jiang Xin submitted a separate memorial asking that Vice Commanders Zu Kefan and Liu Tianlu first take the two cities of Song and Xing, after which Jinzhou would fall of itself.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year, Cunren joined Vice Commanders Zhang Hongmo, Assistant Commander Gao Guanghui, and Battalion Commander Fang Xiank in a joint memorial urging an immediate advance. Assistant Commander Jiang Xin submitted a separate memorial proposing that Vice Commanders Zu Kefan and Liu Tianlu first seize the twin fortresses of Song and Xing—then Jinzhou would collapse on its own.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，新復請進兵，洪謨等及新皆大凌河降將也。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, Jiang Xin again urged an advance; Hongmo and the others, like Jiang, were all surrendering generals from Daling River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year Jiang Xin again pressed for an advance. Hongmo and the rest, like Jiang himself, were all former Daling River commanders who had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年五月，始設都察院，班六部上。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Chongde, the Censorate was established for the first time, ranking above the six ministries.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Chongde the Censorate was created for the first time, placed above the Six Ministries in rank.

sentences.zh: 以存仁為承政，並授世職一等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: Cunren was made chengzheng, and was also granted a hereditary first-rank meile janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren was appointed chengzheng and was also granted a hereditary first-rank meile janggin.

sentences.zh: 越數日，存仁上言：「臣自歸國，默察諸臣賢否，政事得失，但不敢出位妄論列。

translations.literal: A few days later Cunren memorialized: "Since I returned to the state, I have quietly observed whether officials are worthy or not and where governance succeeds or fails, but I did not dare overstep my station with reckless criticism.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Cunren memorialized: "Since I came over to this court I have watched in silence which ministers are worthy and where policy goes right or wrong—but I did not dare speak out of turn.

sentences.zh: 今上創立此官，而以命臣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has created this office and entrusted it to me.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has established this post and placed me in it.

sentences.zh: 臣而正直，後之人正直必有過於臣者；

translations.literal: If I am upright, there will surely be those after me more upright than I;
translations.idiomatic: If I am upright, those who come after me will surely be more upright still;

sentences.zh: 臣而邪佞，後之人邪佞亦必有甚於臣者。

translations.literal: if I am corrupt and fawning, there will surely be those after me more corrupt and fawning than I.
translations.idiomatic: if I am crooked and servile, those who follow will surely be crookeder and more servile still.

sentences.zh: 所慮臣本心而行事，人不敢彈劾而臣彈劾之，人不敢更張而臣更張之，舉國必共攻臣，使臣上無以報主恩，下無以伸己志，獲戾滋甚。

translations.literal: What I fear is that if I act according to my conscience—impeaching where others dare not impeach, reforming where others dare not reform—the whole realm will join in attacking me, so that above I cannot repay my sovereign's grace and below I cannot fulfill my own purpose; my offenses will only deepen.
translations.idiomatic: What I dread is this: if I follow my conscience—impeaching where others hold their tongues, pressing for change where others shrink from it—the whole court will turn on me together, so that above I cannot repay Your Majesty's trust and below I cannot act on my own convictions. My guilt will only grow.

sentences.zh: 臣雖愚，豈不知隨眾然諾，其事甚易；

translations.literal: Though I am dull, do I not know that to follow the crowd in assenting is very easy;
translations.idiomatic: I may be slow-witted, but I know well enough that nodding along with the multitude is the easy path;

sentences.zh: 發姦擿伏，其事甚難。

translations.literal: to expose hidden wrongdoing and drag out concealed evil is very hard.
translations.idiomatic: that unmasking hidden crimes and dragging wrongdoing into the light is the hard one.

sentences.zh: 誠見不如此，不足以盡職。

translations.literal: I truly see that unless I do otherwise, I cannot fully discharge my duty.
translations.idiomatic: I am convinced that anything less than that will not let me do my duty.

sentences.zh: 敢於受任之始，瀝誠以請：如臣苟且塞責，畏首畏尾，請以負君之罪殺臣；

translations.literal: At the very outset of accepting this office, I pour out my sincerity and petition: if your servant is perfunctory in duty, timid and hesitant, please execute me for the crime of failing the sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: At the very moment I take up this office, I lay my heart bare and ask: if I am perfunctory in duty, timid and hesitant, execute me for failing my sovereign;

sentences.zh: 如臣假公行私，瞻顧情面，請以欺君之罪殺臣；

translations.literal: if your servant uses public office for private ends, looking to personal connections, please execute me for the crime of deceiving the sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: if I use public office for private ends and defer to personal ties, execute me for deceiving my sovereign;

sentences.zh: 如臣貪財受賄，私家利己，請以貪婪之罪殺臣。

translations.literal: if your servant accepts bribes and seeks private profit, please execute me for the crime of greed.
translations.idiomatic: if I take bribes and seek private gain, execute me for greed.

sentences.zh: 苟臣無此三罪，而奸邪誣陷，亦原上申乾斷，以儆讒嫉。

translations.literal: If your servant is guilty of none of these three offenses yet is slandered and framed by the wicked, I also ask Your Majesty to judge from on high as Heaven does, to warn against calumny and jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: If I am guilty of none of these three offenses yet am slandered and framed by the wicked, I ask Your Majesty to judge from on high and make an example of calumny and envy.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「此或知有其人而為是言。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Perhaps someone knows a certain person exists and speaks thus.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Perhaps this is said because someone knows such a person exists.

sentences.zh: 朕素不聽讒，惟親見者始信之。

translations.literal: I have never heeded slander; I believe only what I see with my own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: I have never heeded slander; I believe only what I see with my own eyes.

sentences.zh: 且朕志定於上，而諸臣蒙澤於下，縱有奸邪，孰能售其術哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, my will is fixed above, and all ministers receive grace below—even if there are the wicked, who could sell their schemes?
translations.idiomatic: My will is fixed above, and all my ministers receive grace below—even if the wicked remain, who could peddle their schemes?

sentences.zh: 」越數日，以阿什達爾漢為都察院滿承政，尼堪為蒙古承政，並增置祖可法為漢承政。

translations.literal: A few days later, Ashdarhan was appointed Manchu chief secretary of the Censorate, Nikan Mongol chief secretary, and Zu KeFa was additionally appointed Han chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Ashdarhan was made Manchu chief secretary of the Censorate, Nikan Mongol chief secretary, and Zu KeFa was added as Han chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 上御清寧宮，阿什達爾漢等前奏事，上因諭曰：「朕有過，親王以下壞法亂紀，民左道惑眾，皆當不時以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor held court at the Qingning Palace. Ashdarhan and others came forward to report affairs. The emperor instructed them: "If I err, if princes and below violate law and discipline, if the people follow heterodox ways and delude the masses—all must be reported promptly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received audience at the Qingning Palace. Ashdarhan and the others came forward to report affairs, and the emperor instructed them: "If I err, if princes and all below break law and discipline, if the people follow heterodox ways and lead others astray—you must report it at once.

sentences.zh: 若舉細而遺大，非忠直也。

translations.literal: To report small matters and omit great ones is not loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: To report trifles and omit great matters is not loyal and upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 」可法對曰：「臣等惟上是懼，他復何忌？

translations.literal: KeFa replied: "We fear only Your Majesty—what else do we dread?
translations.idiomatic: KeFa replied, "We fear only Your Majesty—what else is there to dread?

sentences.zh: 有聞必以奏。

translations.literal: Whatever we hear, we shall memorialise.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever we hear, we shall report.

sentences.zh: 」存仁曰：「可法言非是。

translations.literal: Cunren said: "KeFa's words are wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren said, "KeFa is wrong.

sentences.zh: 臣誠忠直為國，上前且犯顏直諫，況他人乎？

translations.literal: If I am truly loyal and upright for the state, would I not remonstrate even to Your Majesty's face—how much more with others?
translations.idiomatic: If I am truly loyal and upright in service to the state, I would remonstrate even before Your Majesty's face—how much more with others?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "True.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "True.

sentences.zh: 人果正直，天地鬼神不能搖動，人主焉得而奪之？

translations.literal: If a man is truly upright, neither Heaven and Earth nor ghosts and spirits can sway him—how could a sovereign take that from him?
