translations.idiomatic: If a man is truly upright, neither Heaven and Earth nor ghosts and spirits can move him—how could any sovereign take that from him?

sentences.zh: 」是歲，都察院劾刑部承政郎球貪汙，論罪；

translations.literal: That year, the Censorate impeached Lang Qiu, chief secretary of the Board of Punishments, for corruption; he was convicted;
translations.idiomatic: That year the Censorate impeached Lang Qiu, chief secretary of the Board of Punishments, for corruption, and he was convicted;

sentences.zh: 劾工部奪民居授降人，复別造宅償民，勞民非制。

translations.literal: impeached the Board of Works for seizing commoners' dwellings to give to surrendered men, then building separate houses to compensate the people—a waste of labor contrary to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: and impeached the Board of Works for seizing commoners' homes to give to surrendered men, then building other houses to compensate them—wasting labor in violation of regulation.

sentences.zh: 上以諸臣多未更事，事事加罪，反令惶惑，但誡毋更違令。

translations.literal: The emperor said many officials were inexperienced; punishing them for every matter would only breed fear and confusion. He merely warned them not to violate orders again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said many officials were still inexperienced; to punish them for every fault would only breed fear and confusion. He merely warned them not to violate orders again.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，可法、存仁疏言：「禮部行考試，令奴僕不得與。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, KeFa and Cunren memorialised: "The Board of Rites is conducting examinations and has barred bond-servants from taking part.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year KeFa and Cunren memorialised: "The Board of Rites is holding examinations and has barred bond-servants from taking part.

sentences.zh: 上前歲試士，奴僕有中式者，別以人畀其主。

translations.literal: Last year when Your Majesty tested scholars, bond-servants who passed were replaced with other men given to their masters.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, when Your Majesty tested scholars, bond-servants who passed were replaced with other men given to their masters.

sentences.zh: 今忽更此制，臣等竊謂奴僕宜令與試，但限以十人為額。

translations.literal: Now this rule is suddenly changed. We venture to suggest bond-servants should be allowed to sit the exams, but with a quota of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Now this rule is suddenly changed. We venture to suggest that bond-servants be allowed to sit the examinations, but with a quota of ten.

sentences.zh: 苟十人皆才，何惜以十人易之？

translations.literal: If all ten are talented, why hesitate to exchange them for ten others?
translations.idiomatic: If all ten are talented, why hesitate to exchange ten men for ten?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「昔取遼東，良民多為奴僕。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When we took Liaodong, many good commoners became bond-servants.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When we took Liaodong, many good commoners were made bond-servants.

sentences.zh: 朕令諸王下至民家，皆察而出之，復為良民。

translations.literal: I ordered princes down to common households to examine and release them, restoring them as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: I ordered princes and common households alike to examine the matter and release them, restoring them as free commoners.

sentences.zh: 又許應試，少通文藝，拔為儒生。

translations.literal: I also permitted them to sit examinations; those with some literary skill were selected as scholars.
translations.idiomatic: I also permitted them to sit the examinations, and those with some literary skill were selected as scholars.

sentences.zh: 今滿洲家奴僕，非先時濫占者比。

translations.literal: Today's Manchu household bond-servants are not comparable to those who were seized indiscriminately before.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Manchu household bond-servants are not like those seized indiscriminately in earlier days.

sentences.zh: 或有一二諸生，非攻城破敵血戰而得，即以戰死被賚。

translations.literal: Some one or two may be degree-holders, but they were not obtained by storming cities and breaking enemy lines in bloody battle—they were granted as rewards for those who died in combat.
translations.idiomatic: One or two may hold degrees, but they were not won by storming cities and breaking enemy lines in bloody battle—they were granted as rewards for men who died in combat.

sentences.zh: 昨歲克皮島，滿洲官兵爭效命，漢官兵坐視不救。

translations.literal: Last year when Pi Island was taken, Manchu officers and soldiers vied to give their lives; Han officers and soldiers sat by and did not rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, when Pi Island was taken, Manchu officers and soldiers vied to give their lives, while Han officers and soldiers looked on and did not rescue them.

sentences.zh: 此行所得之人，苟無故奪之，彼死戰之勞，捐軀之義，何忍棄也？

translations.literal: The bond-servants won in that campaign—if we seize them without cause, how can we cast aside the labor of those who fought to the death and the righteousness of those who gave their lives?
translations.idiomatic: The bond-servants taken in that campaign—if we seize them without cause, how can we cast aside the labor of those who fought to the death and the righteousness of those who gave their lives?

sentences.zh: 若別以人相易，易者無罪，強令為奴，獨非人乎？

translations.literal: If we exchange them for other men, the exchanged are innocent yet forced into bondage—is that not also human beings?
translations.idiomatic: If we exchange them for other men, the exchanged are innocent yet forced into bondage—are they not human beings too?

sentences.zh: 爾等但愛漢人，不知惜滿洲有功將士及見易而為奴者也。

translations.literal: You only favor the Han and do not value Manchu meritorious officers and soldiers, nor those who are exchanged and enslaved.
translations.idiomatic: You favor the Han alone and do not value Manchu's meritorious officers and soldiers, nor those exchanged and forced into bondage.

sentences.zh: 」可法、存仁引罪謝。

translations.literal: KeFa and Cunren acknowledged their fault and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: KeFa and Cunren acknowledged their fault and apologized.

sentences.zh: 既，复論戶部承政韓大勳盜帑，大勳坐奪職。

translations.literal: Subsequently they again impeached Han Daxun, chief secretary of the Board of Revenue, for embezzling treasury funds; Daxun was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Later they again impeached Han Daxun, chief secretary of the Board of Revenue, for embezzling treasury funds, and Daxun was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 四月，疏請敕戶部立四柱年冊，再疏請誅大勳，又劾吏部、刑部復用贓吏違旨壞法，皆與可法合疏上，上皆嘉納之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, they memorialised asking the emperor to order the Board of Revenue to establish a four-column annual register; memorialised again requesting Daxun's execution; and also impeached the Boards of Civil Appointments and Punishments for re-employing corrupt officials in violation of the imperial will and law—all submitted jointly with KeFa, and the emperor approved them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they memorialised asking the emperor to order the Board of Revenue to establish a four-column annual register; memorialised again requesting Daxun's execution; and also impeached the Boards of Civil Appointments and Punishments for re-employing corrupt officials in defiance of the imperial will and law—all submitted jointly with KeFa, and the emperor approved them all.

sentences.zh: 七月，更定官制，可法、存仁皆改都察院右參政。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, when the official system was revised, KeFa and Cunren were both changed to Right Vice Commissioners of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, when the official system was revised, KeFa and Cunren were both made Right Vice Commissioners of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 漢軍旗制定，隸鑲藍旗。

translations.literal: When the Han Eight Banners were established, he was assigned to the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han Eight Banners were established, he was assigned to the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 大壽既降，復入錦州為明守，攻數年不克。

translations.literal: After Dashou had surrendered, he re-entered Jinzhou to hold it for the Ming; attacks continued for years without success.
translations.idiomatic: After Dashou had surrendered, he re-entered Jinzhou to hold it for the Ming, and attacks went on for years without success.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，存仁疏請屯兵廣寧，扼寧遠、錦州門戶。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Cunren memorialised requesting troops be garrisoned at Guangning to block the gateway to Ningyuan and Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year Cunren memorialised requesting that troops be garrisoned at Guangning to hold the gateway to Ningyuan and Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 四月，又疏言：「臣睹今日情勢，錦州所必爭。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he memorialised again: "I see in today's situation that Jinzhou is certain to be contested.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he memorialised again: "I see in the present situation that Jinzhou is sure to be contested.

sentences.zh: 但略地得利易，圍城見功難。

translations.literal: But taking territory by raids is easy; achieving results by besieging a city is hard.
translations.idiomatic: But raiding to seize land is easy; besieging a city and winning glory is hard.

sentences.zh: 原上振軍心，與之堅持。

translations.literal: I ask Your Majesty to raise army morale and hold firm with them.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to raise the army's morale and hold firm with them.

sentences.zh: 截彼诇察，禁我逃亡。

translations.literal: Cut off their reconnaissance and forbid our desertions.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off their reconnaissance and forbid our desertions.

sentences.zh: 遠不過一歲，近不過一月，當有機可乘。

translations.literal: At most a year, at least a month, and there should be an opening to seize.
translations.idiomatic: At most a year, at least a month—an opening should appear.

sentences.zh: 兵法全城為上，蓋貴得人得地，不貴得空城也。

translations.literal: In military arts, taking a city intact is best—for what matters is gaining people and land, not empty walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the art of war, taking a city intact is best—for what matters is gaining people and land, not empty walls.

sentences.zh: 我師壓境，彼必棄錦州，保寧遠；

translations.literal: When our army presses the border, they will surely abandon Jinzhou and hold Ningyuan;
translations.idiomatic: When our army presses the border, they will surely abandon Jinzhou and hold Ningyuan;

sentences.zh: 再急，彼必棄寧遠，保山海關。

translations.literal: pressed further, they will abandon Ningyuan and hold Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: pressed harder, they will abandon Ningyuan and hold Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 大壽跋扈畏罪，豈肯輕去其窟？

translations.literal: Dashou is overbearing and fearful of punishment—would he lightly leave his lair?
translations.idiomatic: Dashou is overbearing and fearful of punishment—would he lightly leave his lair?

sentences.zh: 事緩則計持久，事急則慮身家。

translations.literal: When affairs are slow he plans for the long haul; when urgent he cares for his life and property.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs move slowly he plans for the long haul; when they grow urgent he thinks of his life and property.

sentences.zh: 大壽背恩失信，人皆以為無顏再降。

translations.literal: Dashou broke faith after his surrender; all believe he has no face to submit again.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou broke faith after his surrender; all believe he has no face to submit again.

sentences.zh: 臣深知其心無定，惟便是圖，急則悉置不顧。

translations.literal: I know well his heart is unsteady—he seeks only advantage; in urgency he will cast everything aside.
translations.idiomatic: I know well that his heart is unsteady and he seeks only advantage; in urgency he will cast everything aside.

sentences.zh: 況彼所恃者蒙古耳，今蒙古多慕化而來，彼必疑而防之。

translations.literal: Moreover, what he relies on is the Mongols; now many Mongols come admiring our civilization—he must suspect and guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what he relies on are the Mongols; now many Mongols come admiring our civilization, and he must suspect and guard against them.

sentences.zh: 防之嚴則思離，離則思變。

translations.literal: Strict guard breeds thoughts of departure; departure breeds thoughts of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Strict guard breeds thoughts of departure, and departure breeds thoughts of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 伏原以屯耕為本務，率精銳薄城，顯檄蒙古，縱俘宣諭，未有不相率出降者。

translations.literal: I humbly ask that colonizing garrison farming be made the main task, leading elite troops to press the walls, openly dispatching proclamations to the Mongols, releasing captives to announce our intent—then none will fail to come out in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that garrison farming be made the main task, that elite troops press the walls, that proclamations be sent openly to the Mongols, and captives released to proclaim our intent—then none will fail to come out in surrender.

sentences.zh: 此攻心之策，得人得地之術也。

translations.literal: This is the strategy of attacking the heart—the art of gaining people and land.
translations.idiomatic: This is the strategy of attacking the heart—the art of gaining people and land.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，復言：「兵事有時、有形、有勢，三者變化無定，而用之在人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he memorialised again: "Military affairs have timing, form, and momentum—the three shift without fixed pattern, and mastery lies in men.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he memorialised again: "Military affairs have timing, form, and momentum—the three shift without fixed pattern, and mastery lies in men.

sentences.zh: 松山、杏山、塔山三城，乃錦州之羽翼，寧遠之咽喉。

translations.literal: Songshan, Xingshan, and Tashan are Jinzhou's wings and Ningyuan's throat.
translations.idiomatic: Songshan, Xingshan, and Tashan are Jinzhou's wings and Ningyuan's throat.

sentences.zh: 塔山城倚西山之麓，自其巔發砲俯擊，城易破也。

translations.literal: Tashan city leans against the foothills of the western hills; artillery fired from the heights can strike down—the city is easily taken.
translations.idiomatic: Tashan city stands against the western foothills; cannon fired from the heights can strike down, and the city is easily taken.

sentences.zh: 既得此城，羽翼折，咽喉塞矣。

translations.literal: Once this city is taken, the wings are broken and the throat blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Once this city is taken, the wings are broken and the throat blocked.

sentences.zh: 兵法困堅城者，必留其隙。

translations.literal: In military arts, when besieging a strong city, one must leave it an exit.
translations.idiomatic: In the art of war, when besieging a strong city one must leave it an exit.

sentences.zh: 錦州雖不甚堅，當留山海關以為之隙。

translations.literal: Jinzhou is not very strong; Shanhaiguan should be left as its exit.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou is not very strong; Shanhaiguan should be left as its exit.

sentences.zh: 錦州遼兵少，西兵多，一人負箭入，群驚而思遁。

translations.literal: Jinzhou has few Liaodong troops but many western troops; one man carrying arrows inside, and the whole group panics and thinks of flight.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou has few Liaodong troops but many western troops; let one man carry arrows inside, and the whole host will panic and think of flight.

sentences.zh: 能善用巧，山海關可下。

translations.literal: With skillful use of stratagem, Shanhaiguan can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Used with skill, stratagem can take Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 」疏末並言烏真超哈每遇番上，輒令奴僕代，上為申禁。

translations.literal: At the end of the memorial he also stated that Wuzhen Chao Ha, whenever it was his turn for palace duty, always sent bond-servants in his place; the emperor issued a prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the memorial he also reported that Wuzhen Chao Ha, whenever his turn came for palace duty, always sent bond-servants in his place; the emperor issued a prohibition.

sentences.zh: 六年，師屢破明兵松山、杏山間，存仁复疏請相機度勢，以時進兵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the army repeatedly defeated Ming forces between Songshan and Xingshan; Cunren again memorialised asking to assess the situation and advance troops at the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the army repeatedly defeated Ming forces between Songshan and Xingshan, and Cunren again memorialised asking to read the situation and advance troops at the proper time.

sentences.zh: 七年，既克錦州，存仁請招吳三桂降。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, after Jinzhou had been taken, Cunren requested permission to summon Wu Sangui to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, once Jinzhou fell, Cunren asked leave to bring Wu Sangui over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 上頒御劄撫諭，並命存仁遺以私書，略言：「明運將終，重臣大帥就俘歸命。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an imperial edict of reassurance and also ordered Cunren to send a personal letter, which in brief stated: "The Ming dynasty's fortune is nearing its end; eminent ministers and great commanders have been captured and have submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an imperial letter of reassurance and ordered Cunren to follow it with a private note, which ran in brief: "The Ming dynasty's fate is spent. Great ministers and field marshals have been taken captive and have bowed to the new order.

sentences.zh: 將軍祖氏甥，雖欲逃罪，無以自明。

translations.literal: General, you are a nephew by marriage of the Zu clan. Even if you wished to escape blame, there is no way to clear yourself.
translations.idiomatic: You are the Zus' nephew by marriage, General. Even if you wished to evade guilt, you could not clear your name.

sentences.zh: 大廈將傾，一木不能支。

translations.literal: When a great mansion is about to collapse, a single timber cannot hold it up.
translations.idiomatic: When a great house is about to fall, one beam cannot hold it up.

sentences.zh: 縱苟延歲月，智竭力窮，終蹈舅氏故轍。

translations.literal: Even if you drag out months and years, when wit is spent and strength exhausted, you will ultimately follow your uncle's old path.
translations.idiomatic: Drag it out as you may—when wit is spent and strength gone, you will only tread your uncle's old road to ruin.

sentences.zh: 何若未困先降，勳名俱重？

translations.literal: How much better to surrender before you are cornered, with both merit and fame intact?
translations.idiomatic: Why not surrender before you are trapped, and keep both merit and renown intact?

sentences.zh: 」六月，烏真超哈四旗始分置八固山，授存仁鑲藍旗梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the four banners of Ujen Cooha were first divided into eight gushan, and Cunren was appointed meiren ejen of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the four Ujen Cooha banners were first split into eight gushan, and Cunren was made meiren ejen of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 八年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗取前屯衛、中後所，加半個前程。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he accompanied Prince Zheng Jirhalang in taking Qiantunwei and Zhonghousuo, and was granted an additional half stipend increment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he followed Prince Zheng Jirhalang in taking Qiantunwei and Zhonghousuo and received an added half-rank stipend.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關，與固山額真葉臣率師徇山西，下府六、州二十四、縣一百三十一，遂克太原。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the army through the pass, and with gushan ejen Ye Chen led troops into Shanxi, capturing six prefectures, twenty-four subprefectures, and 131 counties, and finally took Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he marched through the pass with the main army and, with gushan ejen Ye Chen, swept Shanxi—six prefectures, twenty-four subprefectures, and 131 counties fell before Taiyuan was taken.

sentences.zh: 又從豫親王多鐸略河南，下江南，督所部以砲戰，屢有克捷。

translations.literal: He again followed Prince Yu Duo in campaigning through Henan and south into Jiangnan, directing his troops in artillery battles with repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Prince Yu Duo through Henan and down into Jiangnan, leading his own troops in artillery engagements and winning again and again.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，從貝勒博洛定浙江，以存仁領浙江總督。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year he accompanied Beile Boluo in pacifying Zhejiang, and Cunren was put in charge as governor-general of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year he joined Beile Boluo in pacifying Zhejiang and was placed at the head of the province as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 兵後民流亡，存仁集士紳使撫諭，民復其所。

translations.literal: After the fighting the people had fled; Cunren gathered the gentry and scholar-officials to offer reassurance, and the people returned to their homes.
translations.idiomatic: War had scattered the people. Cunren rallied the local gentry to go out and reassure them, and the populace returned to their homes.

sentences.zh: 七月，疏言：「近有薙發之令，民或假此號召為逆。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he memorialized: "Recently there has been an order on shaving the head; some among the people may use this as a pretext to rally rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he memorialized: "The recent order requiring the shaving of the head may give some among the people a banner under which to raise rebellion.

sentences.zh: 若反形既著，重勞大兵，莫若速遣提學，開科取士，下令免積逋，減額賦，使讀書者希仕進，力田者逭追呼，則莫肯相從為逆矣。

translations.literal: If the signs of revolt are already obvious, it will greatly strain the main armies. Better to quickly dispatch education commissioners, hold examinations to recruit scholars, issue orders remitting accumulated arrears and reducing the quota levies, so that those who read books will hope for advancement through office and those who till the fields will escape the press of tax collectors—then none will be willing to join in rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until rebellion shows its face, and the cost in troops will be heavy. Better to send education commissioners at once, open the examinations and recruit scholars, remit accumulated tax arrears, and cut the quota levies—let men of letters look to office for advancement and farmers escape the bailiff's knock, and none will follow the rebels."

sentences.zh: 」得旨，謂「誠安民急務也」，令新定諸行省皆準恩詔施行。

translations.literal: An edict came down saying "This is indeed an urgent task for settling the people," and ordered all the newly pacified provinces to implement it according to the amnesty proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: The response came back: "This is truly urgent work for settling the people," and all the newly pacified provinces were ordered to carry it out under the terms of the amnesty edict.

sentences.zh: 十一月，授兵部右侍郎，兼都察院右副都御史，總督浙江、福建。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was appointed vice minister of the right in the Ministry of War, concurrently vice censor-in-chief of the right in the Censorate, and governor-general of Zhejiang and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was made vice minister of war, concurrently vice censor-in-chief of the right, and governor-general over Zhejiang and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 時明魯王以海保紹興，號「監國」，其將方國安鎮嚴州。

translations.literal: At the time the Ming Prince of Lu, Zhu Yihai, held out in Shaoxing under the title "Regent of the State," and his general Fang Guo'an guarded Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Lu, Zhu Yihai, still held Shaoxing under the title "Regent of the State," while his general Fang Guo'an kept Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 故明福王由崧倚大學士馬士英，用以亡國，士英走依國安。

translations.literal: The former Ming Prince of Fu, Zhu Yousong, had relied on Grand Secretary Ma Shiying—a reliance that brought about the dynasty's ruin. Shiying had fled and thrown in his lot with Guo'an.
translations.idiomatic: The former Ming Prince of Fu, Zhu Yousong, had leaned on Grand Secretary Ma Shiying—and that dependence had helped ruin the dynasty. Shiying had fled and now clung to Guo'an.

sentences.zh: 是歲九月，國安自富陽渡錢塘江窺杭州，存仁遣副將張傑、王定國率師御之，斬四千餘級。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month, Guo'an crossed the Qiantang River from Fuyang to threaten Hangzhou. Cunren dispatched Vice Commanders Zhang Jie and Wang Dingguo to lead troops against him and beheaded more than four thousand of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: That September Guo'an crossed the Qiantang from Fuyang to probe Hangzhou. Cunren sent Vice Commanders Zhang Jie and Wang Dingguo against him and took more than four thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 國安退保富陽。

translations.literal: Guo'an withdrew to hold Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo'an fell back to hold Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 又令定國出屯餘杭，遇國安兵，與戰，自關頭至小嶺，逐北二十里，斬國安子士衍。

translations.literal: Cunren also ordered Dingguo to encamp at Yuhang; there he encountered Guo'an's forces and gave battle from Guantou to Xiaoling, driving them north twenty li and beheading Guo'an's son Shiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren then sent Dingguo to encamp at Yuhang. There he met Guo'an's army and fought from Guantou to Xiaoling, driving the enemy north twenty li and killing Guo'an's son Shiyan.

sentences.zh: 十月，士英復以兵至，去杭州十里為壘五。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Shiying again came with troops and built five camps ten li from Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Shiying returned with an army and threw up five camps ten li from Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 平南大將軍貝勒勒克德渾帥師赴之，未至，士英引去，存仁與總兵官田雄追擊之，斬五百餘級。

translations.literal: The Pingnan Grand General, Beile Lekdehun, led an army to meet them; before he arrived Shiying withdrew. Cunren and Regional Commander Tian Xiong pursued and beheaded more than five hundred of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Beile Lekdehun, the Pingnan Grand General, marched to meet them, but before he arrived Shiying withdrew. Cunren and Regional Commander Tian Xiong pursued and took more than five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 十一月，士英、國安復以兵至，存仁與梅勒額真季什哈及雄等帥師擊之，敵溺江死者無算。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Shiying and Guo'an again came with troops; Cunren, together with meiren ejen Jisheha and Xiong and others, led troops to attack them, and the enemy drowned in the river beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Shiying and Guo'an came again. Cunren, with meiren ejen Jisheha, Xiong, and others, struck them, and the enemy drowned in the river beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 十二月，士英、國安屯赭山，掠硃橋、範村諸處。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Shiying and Guo'an encamped at Zhushan and plundered Zhuhqiao, Fancun, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Shiying and Guo'an encamped at Zhushan and raided Zhuhqiao, Fancun, and neighboring villages.

sentences.zh: 存仁與梅勒額真硃瑪喇及雄、傑等分兵與戰，國安所將水師數万人殲焉，餘眾俘馘殆盡。

translations.literal: Cunren, with meiren ejen Zhumarha and Xiong, Jie, and others, divided their forces for battle; the naval force of tens of thousands that Guo'an commanded was annihilated, and the remainder were captured or beheaded nearly to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren, with meiren ejen Zhumarha, Xiong, Jie, and others, split their forces and gave battle. The naval army of tens of thousands under Guo'an's command was wiped out; the survivors were captured or killed almost to a man.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，有姚志卓者，為亂於昌化，與國安相應。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year one Yao Zhizhuo raised rebellion in Changhua in concert with Guo'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year a man named Yao Zhizhuo rebelled in Changhua in coordination with Guo'an.

sentences.zh: 存仁遣傑等擊走志卓，复昌化。

translations.literal: Cunren sent Jie and others to drive off Zhizhuo and recover Changhua.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren sent Jie and others to drive Zhizhuo off and recover Changhua.

sentences.zh: 五月，敘功，進三等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: In the fifth month merits were reviewed and he was promoted to third-rank angbang janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, when merits were tallied, he was advanced to third-rank angbang janggin.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣副將張國勳等破敵太湖，獲士英等，戮之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he dispatched Vice Commander Zhang Guoxun and others to defeat the enemy at Lake Tai, capturing Shiying and others and executing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he sent Vice Commander Zhang Guoxun and others to break the enemy at Lake Tai, where Shiying and his companions were taken and executed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，存仁請設水師五千，備錢塘江禦海寇。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Cunren requested the establishment of a naval force of five thousand to guard the Qiantang River against sea raiders.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Cunren asked that a fleet of five thousand be raised to guard the Qiantang against sea raiders.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，遣副將滿進忠等收福州鎮東衛，破海寇周鶴芝；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he dispatched Vice Commander Man Jinzhong and others to recover Zhendongwei in Fuzhou and defeat the sea raider Zhou Hezhi;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year he sent Vice Commander Man Jinzhong and others to retake Zhendongwei in Fuzhou and break the sea raider Zhou Hezhi;

sentences.zh: 遣副將李繡援浦城，逐鶴芝黨岑本高。

translations.literal: he dispatched Vice Commander Li Xiu to relieve Pucheng and drive off Zhou Hezhi's follower Cen Bengao.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Vice Commander Li Xiu to relieve Pucheng and drive off Cen Bengao, a follower of Zhou Hezhi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣副將馬成龍等破敵處州，克景寧、雲和、龍泉三縣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he dispatched Vice Commander Ma Chenglong and others to defeat the enemy at Chuzhou and take the three counties of Jingning, Yunhe, and Longquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he sent Vice Commander Ma Chenglong and others to defeat the enemy at Chuzhou and recover Jingning, Yunhe, and Longquan.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，明宜春王議衍率眾自江西入福建，保汀州山寨，總兵官於永紱擊破之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year the Ming Prince of Yichun, Zhu Yiyan, led a force from Jiangxi into Fujian and held out in a fortified camp in Tingzhou; Regional Commander Yu Yongfu attacked and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year the Ming Prince of Yichun, Zhu Yiyan, marched from Jiangxi into Fujian and held a mountain stronghold in Tingzhou. Regional Commander Yu Yongfu attacked and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 二月，分兵克連城、順昌、將樂三縣，獲明侍郎趙士冕、總兵黃鍾靈等。

translations.literal: In the second month he divided his forces to take the three counties of Liancheng, Shunchang, and Jiangle, capturing the former Ming Vice Minister Zhao Shimian, Regional Commander Huang Zhongling, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he split his forces and took Liancheng, Shunchang, and Jiangle, capturing the former Ming vice minister Zhao Shimian, Regional Commander Huang Zhongling, and others.

sentences.zh: 存仁自至浙江，屢以疾乞休，至是始得請，受代以去。

translations.literal: From the time Cunren had arrived in Zhejiang he had repeatedly pleaded illness to retire; only now was his request granted, and he yielded his post and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Cunren had reached Zhejiang he had pleaded illness and asked to retire; only now was he released, and he handed over his post and left.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，起授兵部尚書，兼右副都御史，總督直隸、山東、河南三行省，巡撫保定諸府，提督紫金諸關，兼領海防。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year he was recalled and appointed minister of war, concurrently vice censor-in-chief of the right, governor-general of the three provinces of Zhili, Shandong, and Henan, grand coordinator of the prefectures around Baoding, superintendent of the Zijin Passes, and concurrently in charge of coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixth year he was recalled to serve as minister of war, concurrently vice censor-in-chief of the right, governor-general over Zhili, Shandong, and Henan, grand coordinator of the Baoding prefectures, superintendent of the Zijin passes, and overseer of coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 盜發榆園，為大名諸縣害。

translations.literal: Bandits arose in Yuyuan and plagued the counties of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits broke out in Yuyuan and ravaged the counties of Daming.

sentences.zh: 存仁聞歸德侯方域才，貽書諮治盜策，方域具以對。

translations.literal: Cunren heard of the talent of Hou Fangyu of Guide and wrote to consult him on strategy against the bandits; Fangyu laid out a full reply.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren had heard of Hou Fangyu of Guide and wrote to ask his counsel against the bandits. Fangyu answered in full.

sentences.zh: 存仁用其計，盜悉平。

translations.literal: Cunren employed his plan and the bandits were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren followed his plan, and the bandits were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 七年，上令疆吏考校諸守令，以文藝最高下。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor ordered frontier officials to evaluate all prefects and county magistrates, ranking them by literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the emperor ordered frontier officials to grade every prefect and magistrate by literary skill.

sentences.zh: 存仁出按諸府縣，廉能吏有一二語通曉，即註上考；

translations.literal: Cunren toured the prefectures and counties in person; if an honest and capable official showed understanding in even a phrase or two, he would mark him for top grade;
translations.idiomatic: Cunren went out in person to inspect the prefectures and counties. If an honest, capable official showed real grasp in even a phrase or two, he marked him for top grade;

sentences.zh: 非然者，文雖工亦乙之。

translations.literal: otherwise, however polished the writing, he would grade him lower.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise, however polished the prose, he marked him down.

sentences.zh: 監司請其故，存仁曰：「我武臣也，上命我校文，我第考實，文有偽，實難欺也。

translations.literal: A supervising official asked the reason. Cunren said: "I am a military man. The emperor ordered me to evaluate literary work—I can only evaluate actual performance. Writing can be faked; reality is hard to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: A supervising official asked why. Cunren said: "I am a soldier. The emperor told me to judge their writing—I can only judge what is real. Prose can be faked; facts cannot.

sentences.zh: 況諸守令多從龍之士，未嘗教之，遽以文藝校短長，不寒廉能吏心乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, most of these prefects and magistrates are men who followed the dragon in the founding struggle—they were never trained in this. To suddenly judge them by literary skill—would that not chill the hearts of honest and capable officials?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, most of these prefects and magistrates are men who rode with the dragon at the founding—they were never schooled in letters. To rank them suddenly by literary polish—would that not freeze the hearts of the honest and able?"

sentences.zh: 」屢遇恩詔，進一等精奇尼哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: On repeated amnesty proclamations he was promoted one rank to jingqi niha fan concurrently with towsahara fan.
translations.idiomatic: On successive amnesty edicts he was raised one rank to jingqi niha fan, concurrently towsahara fan.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，贈太子太保，諡忠勤，祀直隸、山東、河南、浙江、福建五行省名宦。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died. He was posthumously given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, posthumous name Zhongqin, and enshrined in the temples of distinguished officials in the five provinces of Zhili, Shandong, Henan, Zhejiang, and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died. He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous name Zhongqin, and entered the temples of distinguished officials in Zhili, Shandong, Henan, Zhejiang, and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定封三等子。

translations.literal: Early in the Qianlong reign his hereditary rank was fixed as third-class viscount.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign his hereditary title was fixed as third-class viscount.

sentences.zh: 存仁弟子瑞午，康熙間為福建邵武府知府。

translations.literal: Cunren's younger brother Ru Wu, during the Kangxi reign, served as prefect of Shaowu in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren's younger brother Ru Wu served in the Kangxi era as prefect of Shaowu in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠叛，徇諸郡邑，瑞午不為下，死之。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled and swept through the commanderies and counties, Ru Wu refused to submit and died for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled and overran the commanderies and counties, Ru Wu would not bow and died holding out.

sentences.zh: 子颺、瑛、珍、珖、玳、瑜，子婦王、李皆從死。

translations.literal: His sons Yang, Ying, Zhen, Guang, Dai, and Yu, and his daughters-in-law Wang and Li, all died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yang, Ying, Zhen, Guang, Dai, and Yu, and his daughters-in-law Wang and Li, all died with him.

sentences.zh: 事定，贈瑞午太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: After the affair was settled Ru Wu was posthumously given the title Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, Ru Wu was posthumously made Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 存仁孫璲，康熙間以佐領從軍，鄭成功將​​劉國軒攻海澄，戰死，贈拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Cunren's grandson Sun, during the Kangxi reign served as a company commander in the army; when Zheng Chenggong's general Liu Guoxuan attacked Haicheng he died in battle and was posthumously given towsahara fan.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren's grandson Sun, a company commander under Kangxi, fell fighting when Zheng Chenggong's general Liu Guoxuan attacked Haicheng; he was posthumously granted towsahara fan.

sentences.zh: 論曰：國初諸大政，皆定自太祖、太宗朝。

translations.literal: The historians comment: At the founding of the dynasty all major policies were settled in the reigns of Taizu and Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: At the dynasty's founding, every major policy had already been settled under Taizu and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 世謂承疇實成之，誣矣。

translations.literal: The world says Chengchou actually accomplished them—a slander.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages claim Chengchou truly finished the work—a slander.

sentences.zh: 承疇再出經略，江南、湖廣以逮滇、黔，皆所勘定；

translations.literal: Chengchou twice went out as frontier commissioner; from Jiangnan and Huguang down to Yunnan and Guizhou, all were territories he surveyed and settled;
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou twice took up frontier command: from Jiangnan and Huguang all the way to Yunnan and Guizhou, he surveyed and settled them;

sentences.zh: 桂王既入緬甸，不欲窮追，以是罷兵柄。

translations.literal: when the Gui Prince had entered Burma he did not wish to pursue to the bitter end, and for this reason lost his military command.
translations.idiomatic: but once the Gui Prince had fled into Burma he would not pursue to the end, and for that lost his command.

sentences.zh: 孟喬芳撫綏隴右，在當日疆臣中樹績最烈。

translations.literal: Meng Qiaofang pacified and soothed Longyou; among frontier officials of the day his achievements stood tallest.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qiaofang pacified Longyou, and among frontier ministers of the day none achieved more.

sentences.zh: 張存仁通達公方，洞達政本。

translations.literal: Zhang Cunren was thoroughly versed in public rectitude and saw to the root of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cunren grasped public duty and understood governance at its root.

sentences.zh: 二人皆明將。

translations.literal: Both men had been Ming generals.
translations.idiomatic: Both had been Ming generals.

sentences.zh: 明世武臣，未有改文秩任節鉞者，而二人建樹顧如此。

translations.literal: In the Ming dynasty no military man had ever been shifted to civil rank to wield supreme command—yet these two achieved what they did.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming no soldier had ever crossed into civil rank to hold supreme command—yet these two built careers such as this.

sentences.zh: 資格固不足以限人歟，抑所遭之時異也？

translations.literal: Is qualification truly insufficient to limit a man—or was it rather that the times they encountered were different?
translations.idiomatic: Can formal qualification truly bind a man—or was it simply that the times they met were not the same?
